cleared.check: A1: whether an unlock flag, a currency delta or a synced currency can survive from one transaction into another through Nitro's extra transaction types (deposits, internal transactions, retryable submission, auto-redeems, manual redeems).
cleared.result: The state transition runs the ArbOS start hook and then StateDB.Prepare, which replaces the transient storage map, before any contract code runs. Deposit, internal and submit-retryable transactions end inside the hook and execute no contract code. Each scheduled redeem is appended to a queue and applied as its own transaction. Lock.sol:10-27, CurrencyDelta.sol:28-41, CurrencyReserves.sol:15-38 and NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:12-34 therefore see one transaction as on Ethereum. The go-ethereum file was read on the fork's master branch, which may differ from the commit pinned by the release.

cleared.check: A3 and A4: whether any ArbOS precompile can serve as an ERC-20 face of the native asset or as a currency whose transfer succeeds without moving anything.
cleared.result: balanceOf(address) and transfer(address,uint256) revert on every precompile address from 0x64 to 0x74 and on 0xff when called from the PoolManager address. sync calls balanceOf (PoolManager.sol:285, Currency.sol:94) and reverts, so no delta can ever be credited in such a currency, and a take reverts in Currency.sol:64-86. ArbInfo.getBalance exposes native balances under a different selector that the PoolManager never calls.
cleared.source: eth_call on https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc, https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com and https://rpc.elysium.kinetiq.xyz, queried 2026-11-22

cleared.check: A3: native balance credited to the PoolManager without a call, through a deposit transaction or a retryable refund address chosen by a parent chain sender.
cleared.result: Native settlement credits msg.value only (PoolManager.sol:353-354) and sync of the native currency records no balance (PoolManager.sol:281-283). A forced credit raises address(this).balance and is credited to nobody. It cannot be claimed and it cannot make a settle revert.

cleared.check: Whether a parent chain message can debit the PoolManager's native balance by making the PoolManager the aliased sender of an unsigned transaction or retryable.
cleared.result: The child chain sender is the parent chain msg.sender plus a fixed offset. Producing the PoolManager address needs control of one specific 160-bit parent chain address, which is a preimage search. Signed messages use the signer instead. No other transaction type takes fees from an account other than its sender.

cleared.check: A12: who can produce a call from the owner 0x2BAD8182C09F50c8318d769245beA52C32Be46CD, and what the owner and fee controller can do to pool funds.
cleared.result: The address has no code on either chain and equals the Ethereum timelock 0x1a9C8182C09F50C8318d769245beA52c32BE35BC plus the alias offset. Both chains settle to Ethereum, so only that timelock, through each chain's inbox, yields this sender. The owner can only set the fee controller (ProtocolFees.sol:29-32). The controller can set a fee of at most 1000 pips per direction (ProtocolFees.sol:35-41, ProtocolFeeLibrary.sol:8, 25-32) and withdraw at most protocolFeesAccrued (ProtocolFees.sol:54-56).

cleared.check: Permissionless collect on the fee controller contracts 0x6b3c04567cc62fc5d6ab8d50f1bc1dee161eb2cc and 0x6d0009504d129cf5002dba61d9ae8575aa79314c, including a call made inside an unlock.
cleared.result: An eth_call of collect from an arbitrary sender succeeds on Arbitrum One, so anyone can trigger collectProtocolFees. The amount is capped by a checked subtraction from protocolFeesAccrued (ProtocolFees.sol:54-55), the transfer goes to the controller's fixed TOKEN_JAR, and a synced ERC-20 currency is refused (ProtocolFees.sol:49-52). A collection can only lower the PoolManager balance by fees that were already set aside, so it cannot create a settle credit. The Robinhood controller has the same code length and selectors. I did not simulate collect there.

cleared.check: A9: whether gas caps on these chains can make a large swap or a liquidity removal impossible to include.
cleared.result: All three chains report a per-transaction limit and a block limit of 32,000,000 execution gas, and the last transaction of a block may overshoot the block limit. Parent chain data cost is charged on top of execution gas. A removal touches two ticks (Pool.sol:146-238) and a swap loop costs gas per initialized tick crossed (Pool.sol:344-437), so both fit with a wide margin, and a swap can be split with a price limit.
cleared.source: eth_call ArbGasInfo.getGasAccountingParams() and getMaxTxGasLimit() on the three RPC endpoints, queried 2026-11-22; https://docs.arbitrum.io/run-a-node/arbos-releases/arbos51

cleared.check: A2 and A3: the ArbOS native mint and burn precompile as a way for the chain to change the PoolManager's native balance or inflate the gas token.
cleared.result: mintNativeToken and burnNativeToken act on the caller's own balance and require membership of the native token owner set. On all three chains getNativeTokenManagementFrom() is 0 and the owner list is empty. Enabling it needs the chain owner and a 7 day delay.

cleared.check: A2: whether Robinhood Stock Token splits and dividends change balanceOf(PoolManager) between or across transactions.
cleared.result: Corporate actions change uiMultiplier and leave balanceOf and totalSupply fixed. The token read on chain reports uiMultiplier 1e18 with no pending change. The value per token stays continuous through a split because the multiplier and the share price move in opposite directions, so pools see no jump. Issuer burn and block powers are reported separately as a finding.

cleared.check: A7 and A4: Stylus programs as hooks or tokens on Robinhood Chain and Elysium.
cleared.result: ArbWasm.activationGas() is 2^64-1 on both chains, so no unprivileged caller can activate a Stylus program and a contract with Stylus code that was never activated fails every call. I did not check whether any program was activated before the value was set. If one exists, the Arbitrum One finding applies to it.
cleared.source: eth_call ArbWasm.activationGas() on https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com and https://rpc.elysium.kinetiq.xyz, queried 2026-11-22

cleared.check: A7 and A10: the 96 KB contract size limit stated in the Robinhood Chain documentation.
cleared.result: The PoolManager never reads code size or code of other contracts. Hook permissions come from the address bits (Hooks.sol:337-339) and hook results are checked by length and selector (Hooks.sol:152-166). A larger hook or token contract changes nothing in these paths.

cleared.check: A10: support and semantics of TSTORE, TLOAD, MCOPY, PUSH0 and SELFBALANCE, and the opcodes whose results differ on Nitro.
cleared.result: All three chains are at ArbOS 61. TSTORE, TLOAD and MCOPY arrived with ArbOS 20 and PUSH0 with ArbOS 11. The opcodes that return different values on Nitro are NUMBER, PREVRANDAO, COINBASE and BLOCKHASH, and ASSUMPTIONS.md A10 records that the bytecode uses none of them. I did not disassemble the deployed code myself.

cleared.check: A12 on Elysium: the owner path through the Uniswap Wormhole message receiver 0xa9ae0c5eb238a519b7f5af27415eb6dd0744da8d.
cleared.result: The receiver accepts messages from 0xf5F4496219F31CDCBa6130B5402873624585615a on Ethereum, whose owner is the Ethereum timelock, verified by a Wormhole core whose guardian set (index 7) is byte-identical to the one on Ethereum. A forged message would need the guardian quorum. The owner can only set the fee controller, so the worst outcome is a protocol fee of 1000 pips per direction and loss of accrued protocol fees. LP principal and claims are out of reach (ProtocolFees.sol:29-57).
cleared.source: eth_call on https://rpc.elysium.kinetiq.xyz and https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, queried 2026-11-22

cleared.check: A2 and A3 on Elysium: native HYPE and bridged tokens as pool assets.
cleared.result: HYPE is the plain native asset with no wrapper or ERC-20 face in the protocol. HyperEVM tokens arrive as standard gateway representations that only the gateway mints and burns, and Elysium-native tokens need no bridge code. The bridges do not support fee-on-transfer or rebasing tokens. This rests on the documentation. I did not read the bridge contracts.

cleared.check: Transaction filtering and native token management on Arbitrum One.
cleared.result: Both features exist in ArbOS 61 and both are off: no filterers, filtering time 0, no native token owners, management time 0. Turning either on needs a chain owner call and a 7 day delay.

cleared.check: Whether the four fixed transient slots match their stated derivations and whether a per account delta slot can collide with them.
cleared.result: I computed keccak256 of 'ReservesOf', 'Currency', 'NonzeroDeltaCount' and 'Unlocked' minus one with a keccak implementation written for this review. All four equal the constants in the source. Delta slots are keccak256 of the 64 byte pair (target, currency), and getDelta and applyDelta pass the arguments to _computeSlot in the same order, so a collision with a fixed slot or between two pairs needs a hash collision.

cleared.check: Sign and direction of every delta, which account is credited or debited, and whether unlock can return with an open delta.
cleared.result: take and mint debit msg.sender (PoolManager.sol:294, 326). settle credits the named recipient with msg.value or with the checked balance increase since sync (349-364). burn credits msg.sender and burns from an account that _burnFrom checks for operator status or allowance (332-336, ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22). clear removes only an exact positive delta (310-319). donate debits the donor (268-270, Pool.sol:471). Swap and liquidity deltas go to msg.sender after the hook share is split off (181-183, 224-226). _accountDelta adds with checked int256 arithmetic and moves the nonzero counter only on a transition to or from zero (368-378, CurrencyDelta.sol:37). unlock reverts unless the counter is zero and then clears the flag (112-113). I found no path that creates a positive delta without a payment, a burned claim or a matching pool obligation.

cleared.check: Access control on every external function of the PoolManager, and what the owner and the fee controller can reach.
cleared.result: unlock, initialize, sync and the ERC-6909 token functions are open by design. modifyLiquidity, swap, donate, take, settle, settleFor, clear, mint and burn require the unlocked flag. updateDynamicLPFee requires msg.sender to be the pool's hook and a dynamic fee pool. setProtocolFee and collectProtocolFees require msg.sender to be protocolFeeController. setProtocolFeeController uses onlyOwner from solmate Owned. The controller can set a fee of at most 1000 pips per direction and can withdraw at most protocolFeesAccrued, with a checked subtraction. src has no upgrade, pause or general withdrawal function. lib/solmate is an empty directory in this checkout, so I could not read Owned.sol; a fetch of the pinned file was refused by this session's permission system. As a substitute I ran read only calls on all 21 deployed PoolManagers: storage slot 0 equals the owner and slot 2 equals the fee controller recorded in networks.json, setProtocolFeeController and transferOwnership from a random address revert with an Error(string), and collectProtocolFees from a random address reverts with InvalidCaller (0x48f5c3ed). That shows the deployed contracts gate these functions. It does not show which Owned.sol the CTF build will compile against.
cleared.source: src/PoolManager.sol:96-99, 339-346; src/ProtocolFees.sol:29-57; src/libraries/ProtocolFeeLibrary.sol:8-32; rpc: eth_call and extsload reads against the PoolManager address on each of the 21 rpc URLs in research/network-risk/state/networks.json, run 2026-11-22

cleared.check: Whether sync, which runs while the manager is locked and whose result survives after unlock returns, lets one party collect a credit for tokens another party paid, under the rule that transient storage is cleared at the end of each transaction.
cleared.result: After unlock returns, the lock flag is false and every delta is zero. The synced currency and reserves are the only transient values that can remain. A credit from settle is the balance increase since the most recent sync of that currency (PoolManager.sol:358-360), sync overwrites both slots (286) and an ERC-20 settle resets the currency (361). A payer that syncs immediately before its transfer and settles immediately after leaves no window for another party. A stale sync by an earlier party can only make a later native settle with value revert (356) or make the later party's own sync replace it. The balance can also not fall between sync and settle through fee collection of that ERC-20 (ProtocolFees.sol:49-52), and a take in between makes settle revert on the checked subtraction (360). This holds only while transient storage is cleared between transactions (EIP-1153). If a network kept transient storage across transactions, a party could sync a token, wait, and later settle the whole net inflow since that sync; see the lead on this.

cleared.check: Whether calling collectProtocolFees while the manager is unlocked, at a moment chosen by an unprivileged party through a permissionless fee controller, can move funds to that party or strand another party's payment. This answers the leads raised by the ethereum-reference, established-l1, arbitrum-family and high-throughput units.
cleared.result: My reading agrees with theirs. The function lowers protocolFeesAccrued and the balance by the same amount and sends the tokens to the recipient the controller names. It changes no delta. Collection of an ERC-20 that is currently synced reverts in both lock states, so the settle that follows a sync cannot be shortened. Native settlement uses msg.value and no balance reading. On a network where an ERC-20 mirrors the native balance, collecting native fees while that ERC-20 is synced is not blocked by the check at ProtocolFees.sol:49, and it would lower the next settle of that ERC-20 by the collected amount. The party that pays for that is whoever settles next after its own sync, and a payer who syncs, transfers and settles without an external call in between cannot be interleaved. I found no gain for the caller.

cleared.check: Code level check of a native asset that also has an ERC-20 face whose balanceOf mirrors the native balance: can one deposit be credited twice, once as address(0) and once as the ERC-20.
cleared.result: A native credit needs the synced currency to be address(0) and uses msg.value (PoolManager.sol:353-354). An ERC-20 credit needs that ERC-20 to be synced and rejects any msg.value (356). The two conditions exclude each other inside one settle call. The PoolManager has no receive or fallback function, so settle and settleFor are the only calls that can carry value. I walked the orders sync, take, transfer and settle across both faces: each unit that enters is credited once in one currency id and each unit that leaves is debited once. test/Sync.t.sol:255-275 expects the same revert. Whether a network has such a token, and what else can move its balance, is for the network units.

cleared.check: A currency address with no code (A4): can take or mint create value from it.
cleared.result: take on a codeless currency returns success and moves nothing (Currency.sol:64-74), and it debits the caller. A credit needs settle, and settle needs sync, which calls balanceOf through a high level call. Solidity skips the extcodesize check there only because it decodes the return data, and decoding empty return data reverts. So no positive delta and no ERC-6909 claim can be created for a codeless currency, and a pool on it can hold no liquidity. If code is removed from a token after deposits, takes report success while delivering nothing; that case depends on the network and is covered under A7.

cleared.check: Order of state updates around external calls: native and ERC-20 payouts, hook calls, the unlock callback and fee collection.
cleared.result: take records the debit before the transfer (PoolManager.sol:294-295). collectProtocolFees lowers the accrued amount before the transfer (ProtocolFees.sol:55-56). Pool state is read after the before hooks return (PoolManager.sol:156-159, 202-206, 266-268) and is fully written before the after hooks run. A hook or payee that re-enters meets consistent state and only adds deltas of its own, which it must settle. The ERC-20 transfer assembly evaluates the call before it reads returndatasize, as its comment says, because Yul evaluates arguments right to left.

cleared.check: Hook return deltas: can a hook move value out of a pool it is not attached to, or change the pool's own obligations.
cleared.result: In every hook path the caller's delta is the pool delta minus the hook delta and the hook is credited the hook delta (Hooks.sol:230, 242, 305-313; PoolManager.sol:181-183, 224-226), so the two always sum to what the pool computed. The beforeSwap specified delta changes the amount sent to the pool and is rejected if it flips exact input to exact output or back (Hooks.sol:273-279). Return deltas are read only when the matching flag bit is set, and those bits are rejected at initialize unless the action bit is set too (Hooks.sol:109-120). The fee override is used only for dynamic fee pools and is validated against 1,000,000 (Hooks.sol:263, Pool.sol:303-305).

cleared.check: Rounding direction in every swap and liquidity step, and whether the unchecked protocol fee subtraction at Pool.sol:395 can underflow.
cleared.result: Input amounts and amounts owed on adding liquidity round up, outputs and amounts paid on removal round down, and the next price rounds toward less movement for exact input and more for exact output (SwapMath.sol:63-105, SqrtPriceMath.sol:31-120, 188-288). The protocol share is floor((amountIn + feeAmount) * protocolFee / 1e6), and feeAmount is at least (amountIn + feeAmount) * swapFee / 1e6 in both branches of computeSwapStep with swapFee >= protocolFee, so the subtraction cannot underflow. I transcribed Pool, SwapMath, SqrtPriceMath, TickBitmap and Position into Python line by line. The transcription reproduces every concrete vector in test/libraries/SwapMath.t.sol and SqrtPriceMath.t.sol and the Swap event values in test/DynamicFees.t.sol:185-255. In 4,800 random sequences of adds, removals, swaps and donations across tick spacings 1 to 32767, fees 0 to 100 percent and protocol fees 0 to 1000, the pool never owed more than it had received, during the run or after all positions were withdrawn. This is evidence about my transcription; I could not run forge.

cleared.check: TickMath and BitMath magic numbers, tick and price bounds, and the round trip between ticks and prices.
cleared.result: Each of the 20 multipliers in getSqrtPriceAtTick is within 0.5 of 2^128 / sqrt(1.0001)^(2^i) at 120 digit precision. MIN_SQRT_PRICE and MAX_SQRT_PRICE equal the function's output at MIN_TICK and MAX_TICK. 1.0001^887272 <= 2^128 < 1.0001^887273. The log constant 255738958999603826347141 is 2^64 / log2(sqrt(1.0001)) rounded. A Python transcription of getTickAtSqrtPrice returned the greatest tick at or below the price for about 66,000 ticks, at the tick price, one below it and at a random price inside the tick, including both ends of the range, and rejected 0, MIN_SQRT_PRICE - 1 and MAX_SQRT_PRICE. mostSignificantBit and leastSignificantBit matched a reference on all single bit values and 200,000 random values.

cleared.check: Tick spacing bounds, bitmap arithmetic, the liquidity cap per tick and overflow of in range liquidity.
cleared.result: Spacing is limited to 1 through 32767 at initialize (PoolManager.sol:119-120). With those bounds the unchecked int24 products in nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord stay within plus or minus 256 * 32767, which fits int24, and the swap loop clamps the result to MIN_TICK and MAX_TICK (Pool.sol:351-356). flipTick rejects ticks that are not multiples of the spacing (TickBitmap.sol:57-63). tickSpacingToMaxLiquidityPerTick matches the seven values in test/Tick.t.sol:115-161 and never undercounts ticks, so the sum of liquidity over all ticks fits uint128, and addDelta reverts on overflow or underflow (LiquidityMath.sol:10-18). The cap applies only when liquidity is added (Pool.sol:165-173). A party can fill one tick to the cap at the far ends of the range for very little: at spacing 60 the lowest usable tick takes about 1.9e12 base units of currency1 and the highest about 1.9e12 base units of currency0, by my calculation with the transcribed math, and the party can withdraw them later. While the tick is full, nobody else can add a position that uses it, which includes full range positions. Removal is never gated by the cap, so this blocks deposits and does not freeze or take funds.

cleared.check: Price limit bounds and tick bookkeeping at range ends and at tick boundaries.
cleared.result: A zeroForOne limit must be above MIN_SQRT_PRICE and a oneForZero limit below MAX_SQRT_PRICE (Pool.sol:322-338), so the price never reaches either bound through a swap and getTickAtSqrtPrice always accepts the resulting price. When a zeroForOne swap ends exactly on a tick, slot0.tick is one below the tick of the price (Pool.sol:431). I traced the next oneForZero swap and a liquidity add at that tick: the swap crosses the tick again with a zero amount step and restores liquidity, and the add is treated as out of range at exactly the lower price, which is consistent. The swap loop over empty ranges can be split across transactions by choosing a nearer price limit, and liquidity removal has no loop. A long traversal costs gas and locks no funds.

cleared.check: Masks, shifts and packing: Slot0, BalanceDelta, BeforeSwapDelta, the tick info slot, the position hash, address masks and fee flags.
cleared.result: Slot0 fields sit at offsets 0, 160, 184 and 208 with 160 and 24 bit masks and do not overlap. The 160 bit mask constant has exactly 40 hex digits of f. BalanceDelta and BeforeSwapDelta put the first int128 in the upper half and read it back with sar 128 and signextend 15. updateTick packs liquidityGross in the low half and liquidityNet in the high half, which matches the struct order. The position hash covers 58 bytes laid out as owner, tickLower, tickUpper, salt, and later writes overwrite the sign extension bytes of earlier ones. The 14 hook flags are distinct bits under a 14 bit mask. The dynamic fee flag is bit 23, the override flag bit 22 and the remove mask is its complement in 24 bits. Custom error selectors hard coded in assembly match keccak of their signatures. The ERC-20 transfer selector is 0xa9059cbb and the ERC-6909 interface id 0x0f632fb3 equals the xor of the seven selectors.

cleared.check: Fee bounds: LP fee, protocol fee, the combined swap fee and the 100 percent case.
cleared.result: A static LP fee above 1,000,000 is rejected at initialize, a dynamic fee update and a hook override are validated against the same bound, and the dynamic flag must equal 0x800000 exactly. Each direction of the protocol fee must be below 1001. calculateSwapFee gives at most 1,000,000. At a combined fee of 1,000,000 an exact output swap reverts and an exact input swap takes the whole input as fee without dividing by zero (SwapMath.sol:72-74). A 100 percent fee affects swappers of that pool and does not block liquidity removal.

cleared.check: ERC-6909 claims: transfer, transferFrom, allowance and operator logic, id truncation in mint and burn, and unchecked blocks.
cleared.result: transfer and transferFrom use checked subtraction on the sender balance, and transferFrom and _burnFrom lower a finite allowance unless the caller is the owner or an operator. mint and burn convert the id to a currency by truncating to 160 bits and use the truncated id for both the delta and the token balance, so an id with high bits set maps to the same claim as its low 160 bits. The unchecked block in mint covers only the negation, since called functions do not inherit it.

cleared.check: NoDelegateCall coverage and the raw storage readers.
cleared.result: initialize, modifyLiquidity, swap and donate carry noDelegateCall. The other functions do not, and a delegatecall into them runs against the calling contract's storage and balance, which cannot change the PoolManager's state. extsload and exttload are view functions that only load and return slots.

cleared.check: Fee growth accounting: can a position be credited fees that were not paid into its range, or can the unchecked fee growth subtraction produce a large false credit.
cleared.result: getFeeGrowthInside matches the three cases of below, inside and above the range. A tick's outside value is set only when its gross liquidity was zero and is cleared only when gross liquidity returns to zero, so it cannot be reset while a position with liquidity refers to it. A new position starts with zero liquidity, so its first update pays nothing and stores the checkpoint. A slightly negative difference wraps to a value near 2^256, and its product with any liquidity of 1 or more is far above 2^127 after the division by 2^128, so the int128 cast reverts and a false small credit cannot appear. Donations go only to liquidity in range at slot0.tick and the donor is debited the full amount.

cleared.check: Hidden characters and unused block context in the reviewed sources.
cleared.result: Non ASCII bytes appear only inside comments in FullMath.sol, UnsafeMath.sol and Pool.sol. The non test sources contain no use of block fields, tx.origin, CREATE, SELFDESTRUCT or delegatecall, and no receive or fallback function.

cleared.check: Second independent line by line read of the 18 files of this unit: sign and direction of every delta, rounding direction of every math step, comparison operators, bounds on ticks, prices, fees and liquidity, unchecked blocks, casts and assembly.
cleared.result: I found no line in these files that lets a caller take funds or block a withdrawal for a token whose supply in base units is below 2^127. Amounts owed by a caller round up and amounts paid to a caller round down in SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta and getAmount1Delta (signed versions at lines 261-288), in SwapMath.computeSwapStep (input with roundUp true at lines 66-68 and 100-102, output with roundUp false at lines 84-90) and in Position.update (floor at lines 93-96). The next price rounds toward less movement for an exact input and toward more movement for an exact output (SqrtPriceMath.sol:146-148, 175-177). Pool.swap debits the specified side and credits the calculated side with the signs the PoolManager expects (Pool.sol:371-382, 451-462), crosses a tick with the fee growth of the input currency taken from the running value (416-420) and negates liquidityNet only when moving left (424). updateTick and getFeeGrowthInside use the same convention for growth below a tick (535, 498-509). The per tick cap is checked only when liquidity is added (165-173), so it cannot block a removal. I could not compile or run the code because forge and solc are not installed, so this is a statement about the source text and about my transcription of it.

cleared.check: Solvency of the pool math under random use: can any sequence of liquidity adds, removals, swaps and donations leave a pool owing more than it received.
cleared.result: I transcribed FullMath, UnsafeMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap, LiquidityMath, Position and Pool into Python with 256 bit wrapping, separately from the transcription the accounting unit describes. I ran 28,000 random sequences of 5 to 60 operations with tick spacings 1, 10, 60, 200 and 32767 and one spacing above the allowed maximum (295757), starting prices over the whole tick range including the 2,000 ticks next to each end, LP fees from 0 to 1,000,000, protocol fees from 0 to 1000 per direction, exact input and exact output swaps of up to 2^120 units with near and far price limits, and donations. After every operation the price stayed in [MIN_SQRT_PRICE, MAX_SQRT_PRICE), slot0.tick equalled getTickAtSqrtPrice of the price or one less with the price exactly on that tick, and pool liquidity equalled the sum of the positions whose range contains slot0.tick. Every swap had a non positive input delta and a non negative output delta. At the end of every sequence all positions were withdrawn, every tick had zero gross liquidity, the bitmap was empty, and tokens received minus tokens paid out minus accrued protocol fees was zero or positive in both currencies. No sequence broke any of these checks. This is evidence about the transcription. It says nothing about what the compiler emits.

cleared.check: Properties of a single swap step with extreme inputs, and agreement of the source with the concrete values in the repository tests.
cleared.result: In 371,617 random calls of the transcribed computeSwapStep with prices over the whole range, liquidity from 0 to 2^128 - 1, amounts up to 2^255 - 1 and fees from 0 to 100 percent, the new price never passed the target, an exact input step never consumed more than the remaining amount, an exact output step never paid more than the remaining amount, a step that stopped short of the target consumed exactly the remaining amount, and the protocol share computed as in Pool.sol:391-393 never exceeded the step fee, so the unchecked subtraction at Pool.sol:395 cannot wrap. When the current price equals the target, line 60 infers zeroForOne for either direction, and both branches then return zero amounts, so the wrong direction flag has no effect. The transcription reproduces the nine concrete cases in test/libraries/SwapMath.t.sol:23-176, the rule of test_fuzz_getSqrtPriceTarget on 100,000 random inputs, the seven values in test/Tick.t.sol:115-160 for tickSpacingToMaxLiquidityPerTick, calculateSwapFee(1000, 3000) = 3997 from test/libraries/ProtocolFeeLibrary.t.sol:60 and getSqrtPriceAtTick(MIN_TICK + 1) = 4295343490 from test/libraries/TickMath.t.sol:79. In test/libraries/Pool.t.sol:129 the fuzz test expects InvalidFeeForExactOut for amountSpecified >= 0 at a 100 percent fee while Pool.sol:313 reverts only for amountSpecified > 0 and line 320 returns a zero delta for 0. cleared.check: Whether the int128 casts on liquidity amounts and fees can stop a withdrawal for an ordinary token, and whether the fee cast revert reported by the accounting unit can be reached without paying 2^127 base units.
cleared.result: A removal whose amount in one currency is 2^127 or more reverts in toInt128 at Pool.sol:212-234. The amount scales with liquidityDelta, so the owner can remove the position in smaller parts. In the 28,000 fuzz sequences three final removals reverted for this reason (seeds 12742, 13908 and 111494, all at extreme prices), each succeeded after the liquidity delta was halved once, and every position was fully withdrawn. If principal plus fees overflows in the BalanceDelta addition at PoolManager.sol:171, a zero delta call collects the fees first. The remaining case is the fee amount itself at Pool.sol:192. Fee growth inside a range rises only while slot0.tick is inside the range, when the position's liquidity is part of pool liquidity, and each rise is floor(fee * 2^128 / liquidity) (Pool.sol:404-405, 474-477). The amount owed to a position is therefore at most the fees and donations actually paid while it was in range. A donor who also holds a large position in the same range gets back only that position's share, so the donor's net cost equals what the other positions are owed. Borrowing through take does not help, because the borrowed amount has to be repaid in the same unlock. The solvency check of the fuzz covers the same statement. The fee cast revert therefore needs 2^127 base units of one currency given up by payers, which is possible only for a token whose supply in base units exceeds 2^127 or whose balanceOf is under the attacker's control.

cleared.check: A9, gas caps against the loops in the pool math: can a block or transaction gas cap stop liquidity providers from withdrawing, on HyperEVM with 3,000,000 gas blocks in particular.
cleared.result: Pool.modifyLiquidity has no loop. It updates two ticks, at most two bitmap words, one position and the pool liquidity (Pool.sol:159-236). The repository's own gas snapshots, which I did not re-measure, record 130,613 gas for a removal with an empty hook, 161,276 for a simple add and 292,593 for a new salted position, all through test routers. These are far below the smallest cap in networks.json. On HyperEVM, 80 of the 81 blocks from 51,944,427 to 51,944,507 had a gas limit of 3,000,000 and one had 30,000,000, which agrees with the dual block documentation. The only loop is in Pool.swap (Pool.sol:344-437). It advances one bitmap word per step when no tick is initialized, and a pool with tick spacing 1 has 6,932 words across the whole tick range. The snapshots give about 2,250 gas for the bitmap lookup and 900 to 1,600 gas for computeSwapStep per step, and I did not measure getSqrtPriceAtTick or loop overhead, so a full traversal is in the tens of millions of gas. That exceeds a HyperEVM small block and probably the 16,777,216 gas transaction cap of EIP-7825 where that cap is active. I did not confirm on which of the 21 networks EIP-7825 is active. The loop ends when the price reaches the caller's limit (Pool.sol:344), so a long move can be split over several transactions, and no withdrawal depends on a swap. A gas cap can make large single transaction swaps fail. It cannot freeze liquidity through the code in these files.

cleared.result: A pool can be initialized at MIN_SQRT_PRICE, where the tick is MIN_TICK (Pool.sol:100-107, TickMath.sol:127). The TickMath multipliers equal 2^128 divided by sqrt(1.0001)^(2^i) to within one unit. The slot constants equal keccak256 of their names minus one. This is a self-consistency check and uses no other copy of the code.
