cleared.check: Whether the permissionless collect and triggerFeeUpdate functions of the mainnet fee controller let an outsider take pool funds or raise fees beyond the cap.
cleared.result: collectProtocolFees subtracts from protocolFeesAccrued with checked arithmetic, so it cannot pay more than accrued fees, and accrual only happens in _swap from amounts the swapper owes. The adapter fixes the recipient to the TokenJar. setProtocolFee rejects any direction above 1,000 pips, and the fee value comes from the adapter's override or policy, not from the caller. Pool.swap makes no external call between reading and writing slot0, so a fee update cannot interleave with a swap.

cleared.check: Whether free borrowing of every pooled token inside one transaction (A5) gives an attacker something of value on mainnet that existing free flash loans do not.
cleared.result: Mainnet has no protocol feature that reads a token balance for gas payment, staking or voting within a transaction; gas is paid in ETH only. take creates a negative delta that must be zero before unlock returns, so the tokens come back in the same transaction.

cleared.check: Whether msg.value can be counted twice in native settlement through batching inside the PoolManager.
cleared.result: The PoolManager has no multicall and performs no delegatecall, so each settle call sees its own msg.value once. settle and settleFor are the only payable functions.

cleared.check: Whether the Glamsterdam changes scheduled so far alter how the existing bytecode executes: new opcodes, code size, ETH transfer logs and the state gas reservoir.
cleared.result: EIP-8024 keeps jump destination analysis unchanged and states that contracts which never execute the new opcode bytes are unaffected. EIP-7954 only raises size limits. EIP-7708 adds a log to value transfers. EIP-8037 forwards the state gas reservoir to child calls in full and leaves the 63/64 rule on ordinary gas; core forwards all gas to hooks and to native recipients and reverts as a whole if a callee burns it. EIP-8038 raises costs only, which is tracked as a lead.

cleared.check: Whether block ordering power, reorgs or finality delay on mainnet can split a settlement or let funds leave before payment is final.
cleared.result: Every delta must net to zero before unlock returns, inside one transaction, and a transaction is included or dropped as a whole. Core holds no cross-chain or delayed obligations. I did not fetch a source on finality time or reorg depth; the conclusion rests on the code alone.

cleared.check: A1: whether an unlock flag, a currency delta or a synced currency can survive from one Monad transaction into another, through optimistic parallel execution, a retried transaction, or a system transaction.
cleared.result: The client builds a new State for every execution attempt of every transaction, and transient storage is a field of the per-account state inside it. A retry discards the first State. System transactions get their own State and only run the staking syscall. The lock, delta, counter and reserve slots at src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32 and src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36 therefore start at zero in each transaction.

cleared.check: A3: whether Monad's reserve balance rule can block a native payout from the PoolManager, or revert a transaction because the PoolManager's MON balance fell below 10 MON.
cleared.result: The check skips every account whose code is not empty and not an EIP-7702 delegation ('Skip if not EOA'). The PoolManager has 24009 bytes of ordinary code, so its balance is never tested. A recipient's balance only rises in take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297), which cannot count as a dip. The rule can still revert a user's own transaction when the user pays MON into settle (src/PoolManager.sol:300-302) from an account that ends below its threshold. That is a failed transaction for that user and moves no pool funds.

cleared.check: A3: whether MON has an ERC-20 face, so that a pool on address(0) and a pool on a token could draw on one balance.
cleared.result: No. WMON is a 3249 byte contract with no proxy slot, and its totalSupply equals the MON it holds. balanceOf(PoolManager) on WMON is 927,086 while the PoolManager's native balance is 216,079,353. The staking and reserve precompiles revert on balanceOf and transfer. Native settlement uses msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354) and token settlement uses a balance difference (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), and no Monad contract found here links the two.
cleared.source: rpc https://rpc.monad.xyz, queries at blocks 124417992 to 124420045 on 2026-11-22

cleared.check: A4: whether a Monad precompile can serve as a currency whose balanceOf or transfer gives credit without payment, or as a hook that the PoolManager calls with effect.
cleared.result: The staking precompile (0x1000) and the reserve balance precompile (0x1001) reject STATICCALL, so sync (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288) reverts at balanceOf for either address. Under CALL they revert on the transfer selector, so take reverts at src/types/Currency.sol:82-86. The staking precompile also reverts on afterInitialize and on empty calldata with value, so it cannot be a hook and cannot receive a native take. P256 at 0x0100 returns empty data to balanceOf, which fails ABI decoding. Hook calls carry zero value (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) and a fixed selector, and the PoolManager has no stake or delegation that a staking call from it could move.
cleared.source: rpc https://rpc.monad.xyz, queries at blocks 124417992 to 124420045 on 2026-11-22; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/monad/monad_precompiles.cpp lines 43 to 49

cleared.check: A10 and A3: whether the higher cold access costs (10100 per account, 8100 per storage page) break a payout or a hook call that relies on a fixed gas amount.
cleared.result: The PoolManager passes gas() on the native transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:48), on the ERC-20 transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:73) and on hook calls (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). It never uses the 2300 stipend or a hard-coded gas value. Contracts around it that do are outside the PoolManager.

cleared.check: A9: whether the 30 million per-transaction gas cap together with MIP-8 storage pricing can make a swap or a liquidity removal impossible to include.
cleared.result: A tick crossing reads one bitmap word and updates one tick record. Under MIP-8 that is one page load (8000), one page write (2800), small base charges and at most two new slots at 17000 each, so tens of thousands of gas per tick and several hundred ticks per transaction in the worst case. A swap stops at the caller's price limit (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344) and can continue in the next transaction. modifyLiquidity touches two ticks and one position (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238), which is constant work. The per-tick figure is computed from the documented schedule and was not measured on chain.

cleared.check: Whether charging gas on the gas limit, or the reserve balance precompile, gives a hook or token a way to change PoolManager accounting.
cleared.result: Both act on the transaction sender's MON balance or report a read-only flag. Neither changes a token balance at the PoolManager, a delta or a storage slot. The deltas must still net to zero at src/PoolManager.sol:112.

cleared.check: A12: whether anyone can call the PoolManager as the zero address, which is the protocol fee controller on both networks, and what that caller could take.
cleared.result: No transaction type documented for either chain produces msg.sender zero. Monad system transactions come from 0x6f49a8F621353f12378d0046E7d7e4b9B249DC9e and must target the staking address. MegaETH system transactions come from the registry's system address and may only call the Oracle, pre-block calls come from 0xff...fe to fixed contracts, and a deposit carries its L1 sender. With no controller, setProtocolFee (src/ProtocolFees.sol:35-41) cannot run, so protocol fees stay zero, and protocolFeesAccrued reads zero for the currencies checked. collectProtocolFees subtracts with overflow checks at src/ProtocolFees.sol:55, so a caller could not withdraw more than the accrued amount in any case.
cleared.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/monad/validate_system_transaction.cpp lines 53 to 65; https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/system-contracts/system-tx.md; rpc https://rpc.monad.xyz, queries at blocks 124417992 to 124420045 on 2026-11-22; rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, queries at blocks 32548426 to 32549054 on 2026-11-22

cleared.check: A1: whether MegaETH has an execution context with its own transient storage that shares persistent state with a running PoolManager call. A second context would let a stale sync in one context be paid by a transfer made in the other.
cleared.result: The only nested context is the KeylessDeploy sandbox. It runs a separate EVM with its own journal over the parent state, and the node starts it only when the KeylessDeploy call is the top-level call of the transaction. A contract that calls it mid-transaction reaches bytecode that reverts with NotIntercepted. The outer transaction therefore has no PoolManager activity before or after the sandbox, and the sandbox itself is one ordinary context. Mini-blocks and EVM blocks do not split a transaction, and detention and resource counters reset per transaction.

cleared.check: A3 and A8: whether an OP Stack deposit can raise the PoolManager's native balance in a way that counts as payment, or let an L1 actor call as the PoolManager or as its owner.
cleared.result: A deposit mints ETH to its from account, never to the target. The PoolManager accepts value only in settle and settleFor (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307), both of which require an unlocked manager, and it has no receive or fallback function. Native settlement credits msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354), so ETH that reaches the balance another way, for example through SELFDESTRUCT, is credited to nobody. A contract sender on L1 is aliased by a fixed offset, and an externally owned sender keeps its address, so reaching the PoolManager address or the receiver address as sender needs control of that externally owned account or an L1 contract at the address minus the offset.

cleared.check: A3: whether ETH on MegaETH has an ERC-20 face, through the WETH predeploy or the LegacyERC20ETH address.
cleared.result: WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 has ordinary code, empty proxy slots and totalSupply equal to the ETH it holds. Its balanceOf(PoolManager) is 0.0058 while the PoolManager's native balance is 2.2648 ETH. 0xDeadDeAddeAddEAddeadDEaDDEAdDeaDDeAD0000 has no code.
cleared.source: rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, queries at blocks 32548426 to 32549054 on 2026-11-22

cleared.check: A4 and A7: whether a MegaETH system contract or OP Stack predeploy can be used as a hook, or made to act on a call the PoolManager issues.
cleared.result: The six system contract addresses end in 1 to 6, and each of those bit patterns fails isValidHookAddress (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:111-120). The calls the PoolManager can be made to issue are limited to hook selectors with zero value (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134), transfer(to, amount) on a currency (src/types/Currency.sol:60-73), balanceOf(self) (src/types/Currency.sol:94), unlockCallback on the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:110) and a native transfer with empty calldata (src/types/Currency.sol:48). Each of the last two fund-moving calls creates a negative delta that the caller must repay before unlock returns (src/PoolManager.sol:112), so sending pool ETH to a predeploy such as L2ToL1MessagePasser costs the caller the same amount.
cleared.source: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/system-contracts/overview.md; rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, queries at blocks 32548426 to 32549054 on 2026-11-22

cleared.check: A7 and A9: whether the 98/100 forwarding rule, the per-frame resource budgets, the 200 million compute gas cap or the cap of 1,000 new state entries per transaction can trap funds in the PoolManager.
cleared.result: The PoolManager treats a failed hook or token call as a revert (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137, src/types/Currency.sol:82-86), so a frame that runs out of any budget cannot leave partial state. A swap that crosses ticks for the first time writes up to two new slots per tick in crossTick (src/libraries/Pool.sol:602-612), so one transaction can cross a few hundred fresh ticks before the state growth cap. It can stop at a price limit and continue later (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344). Removing liquidity touches two ticks and one position (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238). The per-block cap of the same size is left as a lead.

cleared.check: A7: whether code at a hook or token address on MegaETH can disappear after pool creation through SELFDESTRUCT.
cleared.result: SELFDESTRUCT follows EIP-6780 since Rex2 and was disabled before that. A contract loses code only in the transaction that created it. EIP-7702 delegation works as on Ethereum Prague and is the same risk class as an upgradeable hook.

cleared.check: A9: whether the SALT bucket multiplier lets an attacker raise storage gas until a liquidity removal or a take cannot be paid for.
cleared.result: Storage gas applies to zero to nonzero writes and to account creation, at 20,000 or 25,000 times (multiplier minus 1). A removal writes at most a few such slots (position fee growth fields) and a take to a new address creates one account. The gas limit is 10,000,000,000 and the base fee read on chain is 0.001 gwei, so even a multiplier in the thousands leaves the exit affordable. How an attacker would grow a chosen bucket was not analysed, because the bound already clears the freeze question.
cleared.source: https://docs.megaeth.com/developer-docs/overview-3/gas-model.md; rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, queries at blocks 32548426 to 32549054 on 2026-11-22

cleared.check: Whether a protocol address with hook flag bits and no hook interface (Monad 0x0100, OP Stack predeploys such as 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000010) adds a hazard beyond what any address without code already gives.
cleared.result: No. For such an address the hook call either reverts or returns fewer than 32 bytes, and the PoolManager reverts at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137 or src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152-154. That is the same result as a flagged address with no code on any chain. A pool created with such a hook address can lock the operations whose flags are set. The hook address is part of the pool identity, so a liquidity provider can read it before depositing.
cleared.source: rpc https://rpc.monad.xyz, queries at blocks 124417992 to 124420045 on 2026-11-22

cleared.check: Do PUSH0, MCOPY, TLOAD, TSTORE and SELFBALANCE exist and behave as the bytecode expects (A10)?
cleared.result: Yes. A read-only creation style eth_call that stores 0x2a with TSTORE, loads it with TLOAD, copies it with MCOPY and reads SELFBALANCE returned 0x2a in both words. The docs state Cancun without blobs and the replay client uses SpecId::CANCUN.

cleared.check: Is EIP-7702 active, which would let code at a hook address change after pool creation (A7)?
cleared.result: No sign of Prague. The BLS12-381 precompile address 0x0b and the P256 address 0x0100 return empty data, block headers have no requestsHash, the docs state Cancun, and the replay client passes no authorization list. A hook address that has code keeps it under the Cancun SELFDESTRUCT rule. This needs a re-check when HyperEVM announces a fork.
cleared.source: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call to 0x0b and 0x0100; eth_getBlockByNumber latest; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/run.rs

cleared.check: Does transient storage (unlock flag, deltas, synced currency and reserves) leak between a system transaction and a user transaction, or between two user transactions in one block (A1)?
cleared.result: No. The replay client builds a new EVM and calls transact once per system transaction and once per signed transaction, and commits state after each (run.rs lines 155 to 168 and 216 to 258). It asserts that its receipts equal the receipts recorded by the production node, so the production node gives the same per transaction lifetime. src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-41, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:15-38 and src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:12-34 therefore see Ethereum's behaviour.

cleared.check: Can a HyperCore to HyperEVM credit raise the PoolManager token balance between sync and settle and be claimed by the settler (A2, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-365)?
cleared.result: No. A credit is a separate system transaction that runs before the user transactions of the block, and the recipient is the HyperCore sender's own address. sync and settle of one payment run inside one user transaction. A credit that lands earlier is already inside the reserves that sync records.

cleared.check: Can any party make a system transaction call the PoolManager, or reach it with msg.sender equal to the owner or to the zero address fee controller (A8, A12)?
cleared.result: No path found. Observed and documented system transactions target the linked contract of a token or the HyperCore sender's own address, and their senders are 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222, a 0x20 system address, or the two AQAv2 addresses. The PoolManager would become a target only if a token were linked to it, which needs a finalize action from the owner in storage slot 0. No sender is the zero address. With the controller at zero, setProtocolFee and collectProtocolFees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:35-57) are unreachable and no protocol fee can accrue.

cleared.check: Does the native asset have an ERC-20 face, so that pools on address(0) and pools on a token address draw on one balance (A3)?
cleared.result: No. HYPE links to the native balance and has no linked EVM contract. WHYPE is a wrapper whose totalSupply equals its own native balance. A native payment is msg.value and a native payout is a value call (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354, src/types/Currency.sol:48), in the same 18 decimal unit as address(this).balance.
cleared.source: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/hypercore-less-than-greater-than-hyperevm-transfers; https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call totalSupply() and eth_getBalance on 0x5555555555555555555555555555555555555555

cleared.check: Do the 3,000,000 gas fast blocks or the 30,000,000 gas slow blocks freeze liquidity removal or swaps (A9)?
cleared.result: No freeze found. modifyLiquidity updates two ticks, the bitmap and one position with no loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238), which fits a fast block. A swap that would cross more ticks than one transaction can pay for can be cut with sqrtPriceLimitX96 and continued in the next transaction, because the loop stops at the limit and stores the reached price (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-439). A sender that needs more than 3,000,000 gas can opt in to slow blocks with the HyperCore action evmUserModify. That costs latency and does not block funds.

cleared.check: Can anyone make the PoolManager send a HyperCore action through CoreWriter, for example add API wallet or spot send, and so control what the PoolManager address holds on HyperCore?
cleared.result: No. CoreWriter's code dispatches only selector 0x17938e13. The PoolManager can call an arbitrary address only with transfer(address,uint256) calldata, balanceOf(address) calldata, hook selectors, or empty calldata with value (src/types/Currency.sol:48, 60-75, 94 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-155), and it calls unlockCallback only on msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:110). None of these matches sendRawAction.

cleared.check: Can the HYPE bridge address or CoreWriter be used as a hook address so that the PoolManager calls them inside a pool action?
cleared.result: No. The low 14 bits of 0x2222 and 0x3333 both set AFTER_ADD_LIQUIDITY_RETURNS_DELTA (bit 1) without AFTER_ADD_LIQUIDITY (bit 10), so isValidHookAddress returns false and initialize reverts (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127, src/PoolManager.sol:126). Both contracts also revert on hook selectors.
cleared.source: src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127; https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_getCode on both addresses

cleared.check: Can a read precompile used as a currency address create credit, since 0x0809 answers balanceOf with a number that grows over time (A2, A4)?
cleared.result: No effect on other currencies. Inside one transaction the precompile value is fixed, so settle computes a paid amount of zero (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). take of that currency always reverts, because the precompile returns 32 bytes that are not 1 and Currency.transfer treats that as failure (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74 and 82-86). Deltas, reserves and claims are tracked per currency address (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-41), so a currency with odd balance behaviour cannot draw on the balance of a real token. The other precompiles tested fail on balanceOf calldata, so sync reverts.
cleared.source: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call to 0x0809 and neighbours with balanceOf and transfer calldata; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/precompile.rs

cleared.check: Does holding a pool token for part of one transaction have value on HyperEVM, given that take lends everything for free inside unlock (A5)?
cleared.result: No use found. Gas is paid only in HYPE by the transaction sender. Read precompiles report HyperCore state fixed when the EVM block is built and do not read EVM balances. Bridging a borrowed balance to HyperCore removes it from the EVM, so the borrower cannot settle, unlock reverts on the unsettled delta (src/PoolManager.sol:112) and the bridge log is discarded with the revert.

cleared.check: What happens if a HyperCore spot token is linked to the PoolManager address as its EVM contract?
cleared.result: Nothing that touches pool funds, in the documented linking behaviour. HyperCore to EVM transfers would call transfer(address,uint256) on the PoolManager, which has no such function and no fallback (the ERC-6909 transfer takes three arguments, src/ERC6909.sol:25), so the call reverts. EVM to HyperCore credits need an ERC-20 Transfer log from the linked contract. The PoolManager emits only the five field ERC-6909 Transfer event (src/interfaces/external/IERC6909Claims.sol:14) and its deployed bytecode does not contain the ERC-20 Transfer topic 0xddf252ad. Linking also needs a finalize action from the owner stored in slot 0. The interaction with AQAv2 sender rules is left as a lead.
cleared.source: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/hypercore-less-than-greater-than-hyperevm-transfers; https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_getCode and eth_getStorageAt on the PoolManager

cleared.check: Can a reorg or equivocation undo a settlement after funds have left the PoolManager (A14)?
cleared.result: Not under the stated consensus rules. HyperEVM blocks are part of HyperBFT execution, honest nodes agree on the ordered list of committed rounds, and a quorum is more than two thirds of stake. Settlement in core is atomic inside one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), so there is no state that spans blocks.

cleared.check: Whether the ERC-20 face of native CELO lets a caller be credited twice for one payment: once as msg.value under currency address(0) and once as a balance increase under the CELO token currency (A3).
cleared.result: No path found. A native credit needs settle with msg.value while the synced currency slot is zero. A token credit needs the slot to hold the CELO token from sync until settle. The slot is a single transient value (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:15-32), sync(address(0)) clears it and sync(token) snapshots the balance at that moment (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). settle with value reverts with NonzeroNativeValue while a token is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:356). The two windows cannot overlap, so each wei that enters is credited once.

cleared.check: Whether take under one CELO face followed by repayment under the other face nets to a gain, and whether a balance drop between sync and settle can be turned into credit.
cleared.result: No. take debits the caller under the currency it names (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). Repaying under the other face creates a positive delta in a different currency, and unlock requires every delta to be zero (src/PoolManager.sol:112). A balance drop between sync and settle makes reservesNow minus reservesBefore underflow under checked arithmetic and the settle reverts (src/PoolManager.sol:360).

cleared.check: Whether the fee currency functions debitGasFees and creditGasFees, which the client calls with msg.sender address(0), can lower the PoolManager's token balances outside a take (A2).
cleared.result: Not reachable. Both clients pass the transaction sender as the debited account, and the PoolManager cannot be a transaction sender because it has code. Deposit transactions do not use a fee currency. Any other caller is rejected: eth_call of debitGasFees(PoolManager, 1) reverts with 'Only VM can call' on USDm, USDT, WETH and COPm, 'caller is not VM' on the USDC adapter and 'caller is not the fee caller' on USDC itself. Fee credits go to the sender, the fee vault and the FeeHandler.

cleared.check: Whether a call can reach the PoolManager with msg.sender equal to address(0), which is the current protocolFeeController on both chains (A12, A8).
cleared.result: No path found. On Celo the state changing calls that the client makes with caller address(0) are debitGasFees and creditGasFees on a fee currency registered by Governance in FeeCurrencyDirectory. The PoolManager is not in getCurrencies(), and any call a fee currency makes onward carries the fee currency as msg.sender. A deposit sender equal to address(0) would need an L1 contract at 0xeeeeffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffeeef. eth_call from address(0) succeeds in simulation only. On X Layer the gasless check is a system call to a fixed whitelist contract. Its caller address was not confirmed and is listed as a lead.

cleared.check: Whether PoolManager transient storage (unlock flag, deltas, synced currency) can leak across the fee debit and credit calls that surround a CIP-64 transaction (A1).
cleared.result: No. celo-revm clears transient storage after the debit and at transaction teardown, and op-geth reset it before the debit. The credit call does see the main transaction's transient storage. By then unlock has returned, the lock is set and all deltas are zero (src/PoolManager.sol:112-113). Only a stale synced currency can remain, and the registered fee currencies are Governance approved tokens and adapters. Whether any of them calls untrusted code during credit is listed as a lead.

cleared.check: Whether CELO borrowed for free inside one transaction through take can be used for Celo governance or validator voting, or to pay gas (A5).
cleared.result: No. Voting power comes from CELO locked in LockedGold, and unlocked CELO can be withdrawn only after a 3 day unlocking period, so a lock cannot be undone inside the transaction that must repay the PoolManager. Gas in a fee currency is debited from the sender before execution starts, so tokens taken during execution cannot fund it.

cleared.check: Whether the opcodes the PoolManager bytecode uses exist on both chains (A10).
cleared.result: Yes. eth_call with init code returned the expected values for TSTORE and TLOAD, MCOPY and PUSH0 on both chains. SELFBALANCE, RETURNDATACOPY, STATICCALL and CALL with value are pre-Cancun opcodes. Both deployments already serve calls: owner(), protocolFeeController() and protocolFeesAccrued() return.
cleared.source: https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call with init code 0x602a5f5d5f5c5f5260205ff3, 0x602a5f5260205f60205e60206020f3, 0x5f5f5260205ff3

cleared.check: Whether block or transaction gas caps can make a large swap or a liquidity removal impossible to include (A9).
cleared.result: No. Celo has a 30,000,000 gas block limit and X Layer 210,000,000, and neither enforces the 16,777,216 per transaction cap because Karst is not active. When Karst arrives the cap equals the one Ethereum already has. A swap can be bounded by its price limit, and ASSUMPTIONS.md A9 records that modifyLiquidity touches two ticks and the bitmap. Pool.modifyLiquidity was not read line by line in this unit.
cleared.source: https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_getBlockByNumber latest (gasLimit 0x1c9c380 and 0xc845880)

cleared.check: Whether L1 to L2 address aliasing lets a deposit arrive with the PoolManager or the owner contract as sender (A8).
cleared.result: No. A deposit sender is the L1 EOA itself or an L1 contract address plus 0x1111000000000000000000000000000000001111. Producing the PoolManager address or the owner address needs control of a specific L1 address. The owner contract additionally requires msg.sender to be the messenger predeploy.

cleared.check: Whether native OKB has an ERC-20 face or another alias that shares the PoolManager's native balance (A3).
cleared.result: No. The custom gas token design keeps OKB as a plain native asset. The two Wrapped OKB contracts hold their own native balance: the predeploy has zero supply and 0xe538905cf8410324e03A5A23C1c177a474D59b2b holds 241,385 OKB against its own supply. A token balanceOf(PoolManager) on either returns the wrapped amount and not the native balance (73.3 and 0 against 321.7 OKB native).

cleared.check: Whether the custom gas token predeploys LiquidityController and NativeAssetLiquidity can debit native OKB from the PoolManager or inflate supply (A2, A3).
cleared.result: No. mint releases native asset that NativeAssetLiquidity already holds to an authorised minter, and burn accepts value from the caller. Neither takes an account to debit. NativeAssetLiquidity holds zero OKB, so no mint can happen now.

cleared.check: Whether the gasless transaction rule changes any balance at the PoolManager or weakens the per transaction lifetime of transient storage (A1, A2).
cleared.result: No effect found. The rule waives the fee for whitelisted zero priced transactions and leaves execution unchanged. The whitelist lookup runs as an uncommitted system call before the transaction. A per block gas budget limits gasless transactions in the builder.

cleared.check: Whether CREATE2 address derivation and hook permission bits behave as on Ethereum (A7).
cleared.result: No difference found. The deterministic deployment proxy 0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C (69 bytes) and Permit2 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 (9,152 bytes) sit at their usual addresses on both chains, which is consistent with standard CREATE2 derivation. The Celo specification index and the X Layer docs list no change to CREATE2. Celo's larger code size limit lets hooks be bigger and does not change how the 14 permission bits are read (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:27).

cleared.check: Whether LegacyERC20ETH at 0xDeadDeAddeAddEAddeadDEaDDEAdDeaDDeAD0000, whose balanceOf mirrors the native ETH balance, lets a caller get credit twice for one ETH payment or take ETH under a second currency id (assumption A3).
cleared.result: No loss path. sync(LegacyERC20ETH) succeeds and records the PoolManager's ETH balance. While that currency is synced, any settle with msg.value above zero reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356), so a native payment can never be counted both as msg.value and as a balance increase. The only way to raise the balance in that window is to force ETH in without a call, and settle then credits exactly that amount under the legacy currency id. That credit cannot leave: take calls transfer on the legacy contract (src/types/Currency.sol:73), which reverts with 'transfer is disabled' when called from the PoolManager address. The forced ETH stays in the PoolManager as surplus that no delta refers to. A caller can only lose their own ETH this way. The contract source could not be fetched, so the behaviour is taken from the predeploy spec and from eth_call.

cleared.check: Whether the native asset has an ERC-20 face on the chains where the predeploy spec lists LegacyERC20ETH.
cleared.result: eth_getCode at 0xDeadDeAddeAddEAddeadDEaDDEAdDeaDDeAD0000 returns empty code on all five chains, and L1Block.isCustomGasToken() is false. sync on an address without code reverts because the balanceOf call returns no data (src/types/Currency.sol:94), so the address cannot be synced.

cleared.check: Whether the WETH predeploy is upgradeable or shares a balance with native ETH.
cleared.result: The EIP-1967 implementation and admin slots of 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 are zero on all seven chains and the predeploy spec lists WETH9 as not proxied. The PoolManager's WETH balance and its native balance are separate numbers on every chain (for example 4,352 WETH and 6,502 ETH on Base).

cleared.check: Whether transient storage can survive from one user's transaction into another's (assumption A1): deposits, the L1 attributes transaction, Flashblocks.
cleared.result: The deposit spec processes each deposit as its own transaction in the manner of an EIP-1559 transaction and lists no change to transient storage. Flashblocks group whole transactions. exttload of the synced currency slot and the unlock slot returns zero on all seven chains. unlock re-locks before it returns and reverts if any delta is open (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), so the only value that can outlive a call inside one transaction is a stale sync.

cleared.check: Whether the ETH mint of a deposit transaction, the L1 data fee, the operator fee or fee vault credits can change the PoolManager's balance outside a call (assumption A2 and A3).
cleared.result: The mint credits the deposit's from address only. Fees are debited from the transaction sender and credited to vault predeploys. The PoolManager is never a sender. A deposit that sends value to the PoolManager must call settle or settleFor, the only payable functions (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307), and otherwise reverts while the mint stays with the depositor.

cleared.check: Whether address aliasing lets someone act as the PoolManager, as the zero address controller, or as the owner (assumption A8).
cleared.result: An L1 contract's L2 sender is its address plus 0x1111000000000000000000000000000000001111. To appear as the zero address a contract would have to sit at 0xeeeeffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffeeef on L1, and to appear as the Unichain PoolManager at 0x0e873fffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffeef3. Both would need a chosen 160 bit address. EOAs and EIP-7702 delegated accounts are not aliased, so they act only as themselves. The owner alias on Unichain and Ink is reachable only by the L1 timelock.

cleared.check: Whether the 16,777,216 gas cap per transaction (EIP-7825) or the block gas limit can make withdrawals impossible (assumption A9).
cleared.result: modifyLiquidity updates two ticks and the bitmap with no loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238), take is one transfer, and a swap stops at the caller's price limit (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344), so a large swap can be split. Block gas limits read from chain are between 30 and 60 million. Deposits are exempt from the cap and bounded at 20 million gas per L1 block. World Chain is left out because its cap was not confirmed. The Base figure comes from https://docs.base.org/specifications/transactions/throughput-and-limits.

cleared.check: Whether the opcodes the PoolManager needs exist and whether OP Stack opcode differences reach core (assumption A10).
cleared.result: The deployed PoolManager answers owner() and exttload by eth_call on all seven chains, and the CLZ probe shows the Osaka rule set. The documented differences concern COINBASE, PREVRANDAO, ORIGIN and CALLER. A grep of src/ outside src/test finds no use of block fields, tx.origin, blockhash or selfdestruct.

cleared.check: Whether interop contracts (SuperchainTokenBridge, SuperchainETHBridge, ETHLiquidity, CrossL2Inbox, L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger) can mint, burn or move balances today.
cleared.result: The five predeploy slots hold proxy code whose EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero on all seven chains. The Lagoon spec that defines these contracts is listed as in development with no mainnet date.

cleared.check: Whether a pool can name a predeploy or precompile as its hook and make the PoolManager call it with harmful effect (assumption A7).
cleared.result: Hook calls carry zero value (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) and the call is accepted only if the callee returns at least 32 bytes that start with the hook selector (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152). A contract that does not implement the exact hook function makes the whole call revert, so no side effect survives. WETH at 0x…0006 and the registries at 0x8453…0001 and 0x8453…0002 also fail isValidHookAddress because their low bits set a returns-delta flag without the matching action flag (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127).

cleared.check: Whether a B20 Asset stock split or reverse split changes balanceOf(PoolManager) without a transfer (assumption A2).
cleared.result: The UI multiplier changes only the derived views balanceOfUI, scaledBalanceOf and totalSupplyUI. The docs state that balanceOf, transfer amounts, totalSupply and allowances stay raw. The PoolManager reads balanceOf only (src/types/Currency.sol:94).

cleared.check: Whether a B20 shaped address that has not been created behaves like an address without code, where a transfer call succeeds and moves nothing (assumption A4).
cleared.result: eth_call balanceOf and transfer (from the PoolManager) on the uninitialised address 0xb200000000000000000001000000000000000001 both revert, so take and sync on such a currency revert. An attacker who creates the token later in the same transaction controls only their own token.

cleared.check: Whether the move to 200 ms blocks and the BaseTime deposit in Denim affects core.
cleared.result: block.number now advances ten times faster and block.timestamp is unchanged. No file under src/ outside src/test reads either value, and the BaseTime deposit calls only its own predeploy at 0x4200…0030.

cleared.check: Whether one UserOp in a PBH or ERC-4337 bundle can leave transient state that takes funds from a later UserOp in the same transaction (assumption A1).
cleared.result: sync has no lock check (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), so an earlier UserOp can leave a synced ERC-20 currency. A later native settle with msg.value then reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356) unless the router calls sync(address(0)) first, which the comment at src/PoolManager.sol:348 advises. A later ERC-20 payment starts with its own sync and overwrites the stale value. The stale reserves can only make a later settle revert or credit a real balance increase to whoever calls settle next, and a router that follows sync, transfer, settle never leaves such an increase unclaimed. The outcome is a reverted UserOp, with no transfer of funds.

cleared.check: Whether anyone can use the protocol fee functions while protocolFeeController is the zero address (assumption A12).
cleared.result: setProtocolFee and collectProtocolFees require msg.sender to equal the controller (src/ProtocolFees.sol:36 and 48). No user transaction or aliased deposit can have the zero address as sender, and protocolFeesAccrued(native) is 0 on all five chains.

cleared.check: Whether the deployed PoolManager is behind a proxy that an admin could repoint.
cleared.result: The EIP-1967 implementation and admin slots of the PoolManager are zero on all seven chains, including the Unichain instance at 0x1f98400000000000000000000000000000000004, and the code length is 24,009 or 24,050 bytes, far above a proxy stub.

cleared.check: Whether Flashblocks, TEE block building or revert protection on Unichain change how core settles.
cleared.result: Flashblocks are preconfirmations of whole transactions and do not change consensus. Revert protection drops transactions that would revert before inclusion. Core settles inside one transaction and has no dependence on ordering or block time.

cleared.check: Can one payment be credited twice through the two faces of USDC (address(0) by msg.value and 0x3600 by balance difference)?
cleared.result: No. A native credit needs settle with msg.value while the synced currency slot is zero (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). An ERC-20 credit needs the slot to hold 0x3600 from before the payment, and in that state settle reverts on any msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:356). The reserves slot is written only together with the currency slot (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), so a stale reserve cannot be paired with a fresh sync. settle and settleFor are the only payable functions and the contract has no receive or fallback. Every inflow is credited to exactly one currency and every take debits the currency it pays from, so the two faces stay jointly solvent.

cleared.check: Can the 12 digit truncation of USDC.balanceOf be used to take funds? Native value can be forced into the PoolManager with SELFDESTRUCT while 0x3600 is synced.
cleared.result: The over-credit is bounded by one ERC-20 unit, 10^12 wei or 0.000001 USDC, per sync and settle pair, because paid is floor(after/10^12) minus floor(before/10^12). The minimum base fee is 20 gwei, so even 30,000 gas costs 6 x 10^14 wei, 600 times the largest possible gain. The dust taken comes from native-denominated claims and can leave them short by less than 0.000001 USDC per event. The PoolManager native balance had a remainder of 970996181983 wei at block 32,554,675, so such dust exists.

cleared.check: collect on the Arc fee adapter is callable by anyone, and collectProtocolFees has no lock check. Can a fee withdrawal in the middle of an unlock profit the caller, given that a native fee transfer changes USDC.balanceOf while 0x3600 is synced?
cleared.result: No profit path found. The guard at src/ProtocolFees.sol:49-52 blocks only the case where the collected currency is nonzero and equals the synced currency, so a native collection can run while 0x3600 is synced. That transfer lowers the PoolManager balance, which reduces the settler's own credit or makes src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert. The recipient is the fixed TOKEN_JAR, a native send to the PoolManager itself would revert for lack of a receive function, and protocolFeesAccrued is reduced with checked arithmetic at src/ProtocolFees.sol:55.
cleared.source: src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57; eth_call of collect from 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io

cleared.check: Can CallFrom, Memo or Multicall3From make the PoolManager see a msg.sender that did not authorise the call?
cleared.result: No. CallFrom accepts calls only from Memo and Multicall3From, and the EVM reverts unless the substituted sender is the calling helper or tx.origin. The only identity that can be preserved is the EOA that signed the transaction, which could call the PoolManager directly. unlock from a codeless EOA reverts when the empty callback return is decoded (src/PoolManager.sol:110). eth_call from the PoolManager address to CallFrom returns 'unauthorized caller'.

cleared.check: Does any Arc precompile or system contract act as a third face of USDC, or do anything when the PoolManager calls it with transfer(address,uint256), balanceOf(address) or a hook selector? take lets any caller make the PoolManager call transfer on an arbitrary address (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297) and initialize lets any address with flag bits be called as a hook.
cleared.result: No. eth_call from the PoolManager address with transfer, balanceOf and all ten IHooks selectors reverts on 0x1800..00 to ..04, Memo and Multicall3From ('Invalid selector', 'unauthorized caller' or a bare revert). Native Coin Authority exposes transfer(address,address,uint256), a different selector, and accepts only the USDC token as caller. A hook call must also return its own selector or the PoolManager reverts (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137 and 151-153). The system log emitter 0xffff...fffe has no code, so it behaves like any codeless address.

cleared.check: Do Arc's opcode differences (PREVRANDAO 0, blob opcodes, absent beacon roots, non-increasing timestamps) reach the PoolManager?
cleared.result: No. A search of src/ finds no use of block fields, tx.origin, gasleft, code size checks, SELFDESTRUCT or delegatecall in the non-test contracts. Core has no dependence on block time or randomness.

cleared.check: Arc reverts value transfers to the zero address, to self-destructed accounts and to blocklisted recipients. Can a third party use these rules to block someone else's withdrawal?
cleared.result: No. The recipient of take is chosen by the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:291) and the recipient of collectProtocolFees by the controller (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44). Core never pushes native value to an address a third party controls. A caller who names a bad recipient reverts only their own transaction.

cleared.check: Does Multicall3From change the lifetime of transient storage or let a stale sync reach another user?
cleared.result: No. The subcalls run inside one ordinary transaction from one signing EOA, so transient storage is shared only among that sender's own calls and is discarded at the end of the transaction as on Ethereum.

cleared.check: Can a reorganisation undo a settlement after funds left the PoolManager (A14)?
cleared.result: No. Arc finalises each block with more than two thirds of a permissioned validator set and documents no reorganisation risk.

cleared.check: Tempo has no native asset. Can address(0) pools, settle with value, or native take create or move value?
cleared.result: No. CALLVALUE is always 0 and the client rejects transactions with value, so the native branch of settle always credits 0 (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354, 364 and 369). No positive address(0) delta can come from a payment. The native branch of take needs a value transfer from an account whose balance is 0. sync and settle never read the native balance (src/PoolManager.sol:281-283). address(0) pools can be created and are inert.
cleared.source: https://tempo.com/developers/docs/quickstart/evm-compatibility.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/main/crates/evm/src/handler.rs; eth_call with value via https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz returns 'value transfer not allowed'

cleared.check: Does any Tempo precompile respond when the PoolManager calls it with transfer(address,uint256), balanceOf(address) or a hook selector?
cleared.result: Only real TIP-20 tokens accept transfer. eth_call from the PoolManager address reverts with UnknownFunctionSelector on TIP20Factory, FeeManager, StablecoinDEX, TIP403Registry, ReceivePolicyGuard, SignatureVerifier, AddressRegistry, TIP20ChannelReserve, NonceManager, AccountKeychain, both ValidatorConfig contracts, CurrentCommittee, StorageCredits, ZoneFactory and ZoneVerifier, and with a bare revert on the ZonePortal implementation and ZoneMessenger. All ten IHooks selectors revert on pathUSD, OUSD and the nine precompiles I tested. A hook call must return its own selector (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137 and 151-153).

cleared.check: StorageCredits.balanceOf(PoolManager) returns a number that rises when the PoolManager clears storage. Can sync and settle on currency 0x1060000000000000000000000000000000000000 turn that into funds?
cleared.result: No. sync and settle can create a positive delta in a currency whose address is the precompile, because the credit count rises between the two reads when slots are cleared. That delta can only be cleared or minted as an ERC-6909 claim for the same id. take reverts because the precompile has no transfer function, and no real asset is accounted under that address. It would matter only to someone who provided real tokens to a pool against that address.
cleared.source: eth_call via https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz (balanceOf returns 15, transfer reverts with UnknownFunctionSelector); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/main/tips/tip-1060.md; src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-364

cleared.check: A call to a codeless address succeeds and take would move nothing (A4). Does the TIP-20 address space make this worse, since token addresses are deterministic and can be named before the token exists?
cleared.result: No. An address under the TIP-20 prefix with no token reverts with Uninitialized for both transfer and balanceOf, which is stricter than Ethereum. Token creation reverts if the address is occupied and tokens cannot be removed, so code at a token address does not change after creation.

cleared.check: Type 0x76 batches share transient storage across calls. Can an unlock flag, a delta or a stale sync leak to another party (A1)?
cleared.result: No. Every call in a batch has the same sender as caller and the batch is one transaction with one rollback checkpoint, so only the sender's own calls share state. unlock sets and clears its flag inside one call (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). The storage credits specification states that transient state resets every transaction under EIP-1153 semantics. I confirmed the batch loop in the client source and did not read the interpreter code that clears transient storage at the end of a transaction.

cleared.check: Fee pre-collection, fee refunds, public fee distribution and guard claims move TIP-20 balances outside ordinary transfers. Can any of them change the PoolManager balance with funds that belong to someone else (A2)?
cleared.result: No path found. The fee payer is the sender or a sponsor that signed, and the PoolManager cannot sign. The refund returns to the fee payer. distributeFees pays a validator's registered recipient, and a guard claim pays a destination chosen by the receipt's recovery authority, so both move the actor's own funds. Outflows from the PoolManager need an allowance or a permit signature it cannot produce, or an issuer role (see the issuer finding). TIP-20 rewards were removed in T8.

cleared.check: Can a receive policy or a virtual address redirect payments that users send to the PoolManager, so that settle credits nothing?
cleared.result: No. A receive policy is set by the account itself and receivePolicy(PoolManager) is unset. The PoolManager has no code path that calls the registry. A virtual address needs ten 0xfd bytes in the middle of the address, which the PoolManager address does not have.

cleared.check: Do 250,000 gas per new slot, the 30M transaction cap and the 30M general gas budget per block make swaps or liquidity removal impossible to include (A9)?
cleared.result: No freeze found. Removing liquidity touches two ticks and one position and clears slots. A swap pays up to two fresh slots per tick crossed for the first time (src/libraries/Pool.sol:602-611), about 500,000 gas, so roughly 55 first-time crossings fit in one transaction, and a larger move can be split with sqrtPriceLimitX96 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344). Filling the general budget costs an attacker about 0.018 USD per block at the base fee, which raises the tip others must pay and does not stop them. I did not measure gas on chain.

cleared.check: Can a reorganisation undo a settlement after funds left the PoolManager (A14)?
cleared.result: No. Simplex BFT gives deterministic finality and a finalized block cannot be reverted.

cleared.check: Can code at a hook address change after pool creation in a way Ethereum does not allow (A7)?
cleared.result: No new way found. Both chains target Osaka with EIP-6780 SELFDESTRUCT and EIP-7702, the same as Ethereum. A hook at a delegated EOA can change behaviour by re-delegating, which is equally possible on Ethereum and is a trust decision for LPs of that pool. Tempo's T14 configurable accounts apply to accounts without contract code.

cleared.check: P1, native take to a special address: does any precompile, predeploy or bridge contract accept value with empty calldata from the PoolManager and return more than the caller is debited.
cleared.result: take debits the caller the full amount before the call (PoolManager.sol:294-295, Currency.sol:44-52). Every ArbOS precompile from 0x64 to 0x74, 0xff and 0xa4b05 rejects calldata shorter than 4 bytes, so the take reverts. The Ethereum precompiles 0x02 to 0x08 accept the value and keep it. The wrapped native token mints the same amount to the PoolManager, which is credited to the caller only after a sync of that token and a settle, and the caller still owes the native amount. The WETH and WHYPE gateways accept the value and credit nothing. EntryPoint 0.7 on Robinhood Chain books the value as a deposit of the PoolManager, which a sync and settle can turn into a credit under the EntryPoint address as currency, and that currency can never be taken because the EntryPoint has no transfer function. In each case the caller pays the full value that left.
cleared.source: eth_call and eth_simulateV1 on https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc, https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com and https://rpc.elysium.kinetiq.xyz, queried 2026-11-22; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/v3.11.3/precompiles/precompile.go

cleared.check: P2, P3 and P4 with a special address as currency: can transfer succeed while moving something the caller is not debited for, or can balanceOf rise between sync and settle without a payment.
cleared.result: No ArbOS precompile has a function with the transfer or balanceOf selector, and all of them revert on both calls. sha256, ripemd and identity return 32 or more bytes for balanceOf, so sync succeeds with a constant and settle pays zero (PoolManager.sol:358-360). Their transfer result is not the value 1, so take reverts (Currency.sol:64-74). ecrecover and P256VERIFY return empty data on the transfer calldata, so take succeeds and moves nothing, the caller is debited, and the debt cannot be repaid because sync reverts on empty return data (Currency.sol:94). The remaining Ethereum precompiles fail on the input.
cleared.source: eth_call with from set to the PoolManager on the three RPC endpoints, queried 2026-11-22; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro-precompile-interfaces/main/ArbSys.sol and the 17 other interface files

cleared.check: P5, a special address as hook: which special addresses pass isValidHookAddress, and what do they return to the IHooks calls.
cleared.result: Of the swept addresses only 0x10, 0x64, 0x70, 0x74, 0xc8, 0x100 and 0x800 have a valid flag combination (Hooks.sol:109-127). 0x10 fails with invalid input length on every call shape, 0x64, 0x70 and 0x74 revert on the unknown selector, and 0xc8, 0x100 and 0x800 return empty data or fail, which callHook rejects (Hooks.sol:152-154). A pool with such a hook has the flagged action blocked for good. For 0x100 the flagged action is liquidity removal, which is the case already recorded for hook addresses without code in the accounting unit of cycle 1. The identity precompile echoes the selector but 0x04 has an invalid flag combination (Hooks.sol:112). No special address returns a delta.

cleared.check: A10 and the opcode differential: TSTORE and TLOAD with rollback, CALL with value, CALLVALUE, SELFBALANCE, STATICCALL, RETURNDATASIZE, MCOPY, PUSH0, gas forwarding, calls to addresses without code and precompile dispatch.
cleared.result: The pinned client implements TSTORE, TLOAD and Call as upstream go-ethereum does, with gas accounting additions only. Eight probes run with eth_call and state overrides returned the same words on Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium and Ethereum, apart from the ArbOS precompile address, which exists only on the three Nitro chains and fails there. For Elysium this covers the RPC node, which runs a locally built binary. The sequencer could not be probed.

cleared.result: StartTxHook runs first and contains no contract call. Transactions that end in the hook run no contract code. For all others StateDB.Prepare replaces the transient map before the call (state_transition.go:636-647 and 737, statedb.go:1599). eth_simulateV1 with a TSTORE in one call and a TLOAD in the next returned zero on all three chains. This confirms the cycle 1 item at the commit the release pins and extends it to Elysium's RPC node.

cleared.check: A3 faces: every way one balance at the PoolManager can be reached under two currency ids, walked through sync, settle, take, mint and burn in both orders.
cleared.result: The only second form of the native asset on each chain is the wrapped token of the Arbitrum token bridge (WETH, WETH, WHYPE). Its balanceOf reads its own storage and its transfer moves no native value, so the two balances are separate. The one cross path the PoolManager can be driven through is a native take to the wrapper, which converts PoolManager native balance into PoolManager wrapped balance one for one. With a prior sync of the wrapper the caller receives a wrapper credit of the amount and owes the same native amount. Without a sync the wrapped tokens become an unaccounted surplus and the caller still owes the native amount. A native settle while the wrapper is synced reverts (PoolManager.sol:356). mint and burn only move claims under the id that was debited or credited. No order yields a credit without an equal payment.

cleared.check: A8 and cross-chain senders: can the PoolManager of the parent chain be driven to send a deposit or a message into the child chain, which would act there under its alias.
cleared.result: The parent chain PoolManager can only make calls with empty calldata, transfer, balanceOf, the IHooks selectors and unlockCallback. The Inbox and Bridge of Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain on Ethereum and of Elysium on HyperEVM revert on empty calldata with value and on transfer from the PoolManager address of that chain. They reject plain value, so the path that exists on chains whose deposit contract accepts a bare transfer does not exist here.

cleared.check: Critic lead from cycle 1: what a filter entry identifies, whether entries are added automatically, and whether an ordinary account can make an entry or a rule match another user's PoolManager transaction.
cleared.result: An entry is one transaction hash. Entries are added by an automated loop for delayed inbox transactions that touch a restricted address, which is consistent with several thousand entries from one account. A transaction touches an address only as sender, recipient, retryable field, call target, created address, selfdestruct beneficiary, message destination, or as an address in a log topic that a configured event rule names. The restricted list is an off-chain hash list that only the operator's provider changes. In a swap or liquidity change on a pool without attacker-made hook or token, the call targets are the router, Permit2, the PoolManager, the two tokens and the recipient the user named, and the logs come from those contracts with the user, the router and the PoolManager as addresses (PoolManager.sol:145-297). No value in them is chosen by a third party. An attacker who makes the PoolManager call or pay a restricted address through take only gets the attacker's own transaction rejected or hash filtered. The finding therefore stays in the operator class. A pool whose hook or token calls or names a restricted address does block its users, which is the pool-creator class. I did not see the configured event rules or the list itself.

cleared.check: A2 on Robinhood Chain: can an ordinary account raise or lower the PoolManager balance of USDG or a stock token without a transfer.
cleared.result: mint, burn and adminBurn on the stock token revert for an arbitrary caller with an access control error, and transferFrom needs an allowance that the PoolManager never gives (no approve call exists in src outside the ERC-6909 claims). cleared.check: Can one owner change or withdraw another owner's position through modifyLiquidity, including by reusing a salt, by passing ticks of another position, or by removing more than it holds.
cleared.result: No. The position is looked up under keccak256 of owner, tickLower, tickUpper and salt, and the owner is always msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:161, src/libraries/Position.sol:34-41). The assembly lays the four fields out as 20, 3, 3 and 32 bytes without overlap, and bytes above the address fall outside the hashed range (Position.sol:54-66). I rebuilt the layout byte for byte and compared it with the packed encoding that test/libraries/Position.t.sol:75-80 expects on 3,000 random inputs, with dirty upper bits in the owner word. A removal larger than the position reverts in LiquidityMath.addDelta (Position.sol:88, src/libraries/LiquidityMath.sol:10-18), after the tick updates, and the revert undoes those. In 6,000 random sequences on a Python transcription, every attempt by a second owner, by the same owner under a different salt, or for one unit more than the position held reverted.

cleared.check: Order of the steps inside Pool.modifyLiquidity: tick update, bitmap flip, fee growth read, Position.update, tick clearing, and the three price cases for the amounts. Covered add, remove, zero delta, full range, one spacing, ranges above, below and around the current tick, and several owners on shared ticks.
cleared.result: The order is sound. A new tick gets its feeGrowthOutside before the fee growth inside the range is read (src/libraries/Pool.sol:160-162, 533-539, 184-185). A tick whose liquidityGross returns to zero is deleted only after the last position has been paid from its values (Pool.sol:187-203). A position that still has liquidity keeps both its ticks alive, because liquidityGross is the sum of the positions on the tick, so its checkpoint can never meet a re-initialized tick. A position with zero liquidity earns nothing at its next update because fees use the liquidity held before the update (src/libraries/Position.sol:82-97). Amounts use slot0.tick for the range test and the stored sqrt price for the in range case, add rounds up and remove rounds down (Pool.sol:206-237, src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:261-288). I transcribed Pool, Position, TickBitmap, LiquidityMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath and TickMath into Python and ran 6,000 random sequences (254,069 operations, 50,789 of them reverts) with four owners, two salts, spacings 1, 10, 60, 200, 2000 and 32767, start prices in the middle and within 3,000 ticks of both ends, swaps, donations and protocol fees. After every operation liquidityGross and liquidityNet of each tick equalled the sums over positions, the bitmap bit was set exactly for ticks with liquidityGross above zero, pool liquidity equalled the liquidity of positions in range at slot0.tick, and the pool never owed more of either currency than it had received. At the end every position could be removed in full and all tick data was gone. A second set of 6,000 sequences without swaps or donations, 3,614 of them started in the state where slot0.tick is one below the tick of the price, paid no fees to anyone and left no owner with more than it had paid in.

cleared.check: Can an ordinary account make a hookless victim position impossible to remove, or leave a tick that can no longer be updated. Listed every revert on the removal path.
cleared.result: No path found for a token with fewer than 2^127 base units. On removal the cap is not checked (src/libraries/Pool.sol:165). liquidityGross cannot underflow because it is the sum of the positions. liquidityNet stays inside int128 because its size is bounded by liquidityGross, and the cap is at most 6076470837873901133274546561281575204 (spacing 32767), below 2^127. The same bound keeps pool liquidity inside uint128 when ticks are crossed. flipTick cannot revert for a tick that was initialized, since only aligned ticks can be initialized (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:47-75). FullMath.mulDiv in Position.update cannot revert because the product of a 256 bit growth difference and a 128 bit liquidity divided by 2^128 fits in 256 bits. The casts of the principal amounts can revert for a very large position, and the owner then removes in parts. The sum of principal and fees can exceed int128, and the owner then collects fees with a zero delta first (src/PoolManager.sol:171). What remains is the known case of uncollected fees of 2^127 base units or more (F-005). I checked whether flash accounting gives a cheaper route to that bound: it does not. An account that is the only liquidity in range can donate to itself at no cost and wrap feeGrowthGlobal past 2^256, as the comment at Pool.sol:80-82 says, but positions out of range see no change in their fee growth inside, and after later tick crossings they are owed only real swap fees (six self donations of 2^127 - 1 units in the transcription, then swaps through both victim ranges). When a victim is in range, its share of a donation is real value the donor has to pay.

cleared.check: Hook deltas on liquidity changes: can afterAddLiquidity or afterRemoveLiquidity move more than the caller's own delta, which hook runs for a zero delta, and what a hook that calls modifyLiquidity itself can skip.
cleared.result: The caller delta after the hook is the pool delta minus the hook delta, and the hook is credited the hook delta, so the two always add up to principal plus fees (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:219-244, src/PoolManager.sol:171-183). The hook delta is read only when the matching return-delta bit is set, and then the return data must be exactly 64 bytes (Hooks.sol:159-168). A zero delta runs the remove hooks (Hooks.sol:201-205, 220-244). When the hook itself is the caller, the hook calls are skipped and no delta is taken (Hooks.sol:171-175, 217). A pool without a hook has none of these paths. The hazard for pools whose liquidity providers chose a hook is already recorded as F-004. One comment differs from the code: src/interfaces/IHooks.sol:50 and 81 say the delta passed to the after hooks includes the hook delta, while the code passes principal plus fees before the hook delta is known. This changes no balance.

cleared.check: donate from entry to the last delta: who is debited, who can receive, rounding, the tick and price mismatch at a boundary, and whether a donation can be redirected away from positions that were in range.
cleared.result: The donor is debited the two amounts, each cast to int128, and fee growth rises by amount times 2^128 divided by the liquidity in range, rounded down (src/libraries/Pool.sol:466-480, src/PoolManager.sol:256-276). A donation reverts when no liquidity is in range. The rounding remainder is below one base unit per donation and stays in the PoolManager. In the transcription each in range position was owed at most its exact share and the shares never added up to more than the donation, across all donations in 6,000 sequences. Positions out of range were unchanged. The two concrete values of test/PoolManager.t.sol:841-864 (34028236692093846346337 and 68056473384187692692674 for 100 and 200 units on 1e18 liquidity) come out of the source formula. Two things can redirect a donation, and both are stated in src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:150-155: liquidity added just before the donation takes a share, and after a zeroForOne swap that ends exactly on a tick, slot0.tick is one below the tick of the price, so the donation goes to the range below. Both cost the donor's intended recipients future income and take nothing that a position already holds.

cleared.check: Lead L-133, second half: is there a hook that must add liquidity on a tick an attacker can fill cheaply. Read the Zora coin hook, which adds liquidity inside afterSwap.
cleared.result: Not affected at realistic prices. CoinRewardsV4.mintLpReward runs inside afterSwap without a try block and adds a position one spacing wide that starts two spacings away from the current tick (CoinRewardsV4.sol lines 134-204, ZoraV4CoinHook.sol line 415 on the main branch).
