cleared.check: P1, native take to a special address: does any precompile, predeploy, registry contract, bridge, wrapper, fee contract or preinstalled contract accept value with empty calldata from the PoolManager and give the caller more than the amount the caller is debited.
cleared.result: No. 365 addresses on Celo and 302 on X Layer were called with msg.sender set to the PoolManager, empty calldata and values 0, 1 wei and 10^18 wei. The targets that accept value keep it (fee vaults, FeeHandler contracts, Reserve, Governance, L1BlockNumber), book it to the PoolManager address (EntryPoints, wrapped native contracts) or start a withdrawal for the PoolManager address (Celo L2ToL1MessagePasser). take debits the caller the full amount before the call (src/PoolManager.sol:294), so none of these gives the caller value. The low finding in this file records the loss to the caller.
cleared.source: https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call sweep, 2026-11-22; src/PoolManager.sol:291-297

cleared.check: P2 and P3, a special address used as a currency: can transfer(address,uint256) from the PoolManager succeed while it moves something the caller is not debited for, and can balanceOf(PoolManager) rise between sync and settle without a payment.
cleared.result: No. transfer returns true only on real tokens (CELO, the Mento stable tokens, bridged WETH, USDC, USDT, USDT0, the wrapped native contracts), where the caller is debited the same amount under the same currency id. FeeHandler, MentoFeeHandlerSeller, UniswapFeeHandlerSeller and Reserve on Celo, a Safe on X Layer, ecrecover and 0x0100 return success with no data, which core accepts (src/types/Currency.sol:68), and they move nothing. Their balanceOf returns no data, so sync reverts and no credit can be created for them. sha256, ripemd160, identity, L1BlockNumber and the deterministic deployment proxy return data that the transfer check rejects. balanceOf on L1BlockNumber returns the L1 block number, which is constant inside one transaction, so a sync and settle pair credits zero.
cleared.source: https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call transfer and balanceOf with from set to the PoolManager; eth_call sync(address) on the Celo PoolManager for 0xfd, FeeHandler, L1BlockNumber and an EntryPoint; src/types/Currency.sol:60-96

cleared.check: P5, a special address used as a hook: does any swept address pass isValidHookAddress and answer a hook call with its selector.
cleared.result: No. No swept address returns data that starts with the called selector and has the required length, except the identity precompile, whose address 0x04 sets a return delta flag without its action flag and is rejected (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:112). The wrapped native contracts, the Celo fee contracts and the Reserve accept hook calldata and return no data, which fails the 32 byte minimum (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152). EntryPoint v0.6 has a valid flag pattern (low bits 0x2789) and reverts on every hook selector. The CELO token (0x2438), its implementation (0x37b1 with reverting calls), the gasless whitelist (0x1b27), the blacklist (0x1727) and 0xfd fail the flag rules or revert.
cleared.source: https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call with each IHooks selector and from set to the PoolManager; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-155

cleared.check: Whether a contract that the PoolManager calls (a hook, an unlock callback, a payout recipient or a currency) can reach the Celo transfer precompile with the PoolManager's balance as source, including through DELEGATECALL or CALLCODE.
cleared.result: No. The precompile requires input.caller to be the CELO token address. A CALL or CALLCODE from any other contract carries that contract as caller. A DELEGATECALL carries the caller of the delegating frame, which is the PoolManager when the PoolManager made the call, and the PoolManager is not the token. The inherited caller would be the token only for a contract that the token address itself calls. The deployed implementation calls the precompile, the registry and the unreleased treasury view and nothing else, and it does not call transfer recipients. An eth_call to 0xfd from the PoolManager fails for every call shape.

cleared.check: Cycle 1 lead: does the deployed CELO token implementation (version 1.2.0.0) contain a function that passes an account other than msg.sender or an allowance checked account to the transfer precompile.
cleared.result: No. The 24 selectors in the deployed bytecode equal the function list of GoldToken.sol at tag core-contracts.v15, which returns version (1, 2, 0, 0). transfer, transferWithComment and burn pass msg.sender. transferFrom requires value to be within allowed[from][msg.sender]. The version has no mint, no fee debit and no other balance moving function. transferFrom with the PoolManager as source reverts on chain, and the PoolManager never calls approve on a currency (src/types/Currency.sol:60-96 holds the only token calls).

cleared.check: Faces on Celo: every way the PoolManager's native balance or a token balance can be read under a second currency id (the CELO token proxy, its implementation address, the four fee currency adapters, the wrapped native predeploy, any contract whose balanceOf returns a native balance), walked through sync, settle, take, mint and burn in each order.
cleared.result: No gain in any order. Credits arise only in _settle: msg.value when no currency is synced, or the balance rise of the one synced currency (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364). One transient slot holds the synced currency (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), and a settle with value reverts while it is set (src/PoolManager.sol:356), so one inflow is credited under one id. I walked these orders. Sync the token, take native, return it by token transfer, settle: the credit is zero. Take native, sync the token, return by token transfer, settle: the caller holds a token credit equal to the native debt and must still pay the debt. Take the token, sync address(0), settle with value: the same with the faces swapped. Sync the implementation address or an adapter, pay the real token, settle: the caller is credited under an id whose transfer reverts, so the credit cannot be taken, and the adapter scales the credit by 10^12 without any way to withdraw it. The PoolManager has no receive or fallback function, and a plain value call to the deployed contract reverts. The wrapped native predeploy keeps its own balance and is a separate asset.
cleared.source: src/PoolManager.sol:279-297, 349-364; https://forno.celo.org eth_call on the PoolManager (plain value call, settle with value while locked, sync for the CELO token, its implementation and an adapter)

cleared.check: A2 on Celo: can an ordinary account raise the PoolManager's native balance inside another party's sync and settle window, or with funds that are not its own.
cleared.result: No path found. Native CELO reaches the PoolManager through settle with value, a CELO token transfer, a self destruct beneficiary or a block reward. Each of these spends the sender's own funds. Deposit mints go to the deposit sender. Fee refunds and fee credits of CIP-64 transactions go to the transaction sender, the fee recipient and the FeeHandler. Withdrawals from the wrapped native predeploy pay msg.sender only, and the PoolManager never calls withdraw. A party that syncs the CELO token and then funds the PoolManager is credited what it paid.

cleared.check: Opcode differential on Celo: does the client change any opcode or call pattern the PoolManager relies on (TSTORE and TLOAD, CALL with value, CALLVALUE, SELFBALANCE, STATICCALL, RETURNDATASIZE and RETURNDATACOPY, MCOPY, PUSH0, gas forwarding, calls to addresses without code, precompile dispatch).
cleared.result: No change found. CeloEvm uses the revm mainnet instruction table for the chain spec, and the precompile map is the OP Stack set plus the transfer precompile. The transfer precompile refuses static contexts, so a balanceOf call made by sync cannot move native value. A probe CALL to an address without code returns success with empty return data, as core assumes for the A4 case. The one address where a plain CALL fails on Celo and succeeds on Ethereum is 0xfd, which makes a take that names it revert.

cleared.check: Opcode differential on X Layer: does the OKX client change any opcode, the precompile set or call semantics.
cleared.result: No change found. revm 40.0.3 comes from crates.io without a patch. The OKX op-revm builds the EVM with the mainnet instruction table and the OP Stack precompile set, and its precompile file has no X Layer entry. The X Layer changes sit in the handler (fee handling of gasless transactions) and in the block executor (the two system calls). Probe calls to 0xfd, 0x0100, the identity precompile and an address without code return what they return on Ethereum.

cleared.check: Cycle 1 critic gap and lead: where does the X Layer client discard transient storage between two transactions of one block, including the gasless whitelist call, the blacklist call, blacklisted deposits and the flashblocks builder (A1).
cleared.result: Transient storage is cleared on every path. The executor and the builder run each transaction with Evm::transact, which ends in the journal's finalize, and finalize, commit_tx and discard_tx each clear transient storage. The whitelist and blacklist lookups are system calls whose result state is dropped. On success they end in finalize and on error the OKX code calls discard_tx. A blacklisted or failed deposit goes through checkpoint_revert and commit_tx. One path does not discard the journal: catch_error for a rejected non-deposit transaction. Such a rejection is raised during validation, before any contract code has run, so no TSTORE can precede it. I did not trace every error variant to confirm that last statement.

cleared.check: Cycle 1 lead: which caller address does the gasless whitelist system call use, and can it reach the PoolManager as address(0), the current protocol fee controller (A12, A8).
cleared.result: No. The caller is 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe, the call goes to the whitelist proxy only, and its state changes are never committed. The blacklist lookup uses the same caller. A call made onward by either contract would carry that contract as msg.sender and would be discarded with the rest of the call. collectProtocolFees and setProtocolFee compare msg.sender with the stored controller (src/ProtocolFees.sol:36, 48).

cleared.check: Whether a gasless transaction can create native OKB or move value that the sender does not hold (A2, A3).
cleared.result: No. The handler rejects a gasless transaction whose sender balance is below its value. It then leaves the balance unchanged, and the call frame moves the value from the sender as for any transaction. Fee deduction, refund and vault payments are skipped, so no account is credited. The earlier bug in this feature left the base fee check relaxed for later transactions of a block and concerned fees only.

cleared.check: Faces on X Layer: can the PoolManager's OKB balance or a token balance be reached under a second currency id.
cleared.result: None found. OKB has no ERC-20 contract on X Layer: no code sits at the L1 OKB address or at 0xfd, and both Wrapped OKB contracts hold their own native balance. LiquidityController and NativeAssetLiquidity revert on balanceOf and transfer. The bridge wrapped tokens and USDT0 answer under one address each in the sweep. Tokens with a second entry point among the smaller holdings were not searched for and are listed as a lead.
cleared.source: https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call sweep with from set to the PoolManager

cleared.check: Known weakness: the reth trie iterator bug fixed upstream on 3 November 2026 (pull request 28264), which can drop a leaf from an incremental state root.
cleared.result: No path to PoolManager funds. The bug makes a node compute a wrong state root, stall or serve a wrong proof. It does not change what a transaction executes. xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1 integrates the fix as a mandatory patch. For Celo two secondary reports state that celo-kona shipped a backport, and I did not confirm which build the sequencer runs. A stall delays every PoolManager transaction and loses nothing, because core has no time dependence.

cleared.check: Known weaknesses of the Celo client and precompile from the last two years: the missing STATICCALL guard in the transfer precompile (Nethermind review, fixed October 2025), the warm slot leak of the fee currency context (fixed May 2026), the June 2026 security review, the node divergence on CIP-64 blocks after a storage migration (issue 192) and the open issues on CIP-64 refunds.
cleared.result: None gives an ordinary account a way to move PoolManager funds. With the guard missing, a static call into the CELO token still reverted at the Transfer event, and the guard is present in the current source. The warm slot leak and the refund issue change gas charges. Issue 192 was a history index lost in a node migration and made single nodes reject valid blocks. The June 2026 review reports no critical or high issue.

cleared.check: Known weaknesses of the X Layer client: the public issue that lists 13 alleged vulnerabilities (issue 276), the tracing failure after gasless transactions (issue 277) and the gasless base fee bypass fix.
cleared.result: None reaches PoolManager funds. Issue 276 concerns node configuration through environment variables, panics on malformed arguments and flashblocks cache handling, all of which need access to the node or to the sequencer's flashblocks feed. Issue 277 is an RPC tracing defect. The base fee bypass let zero priced transactions pass validation and moved no balance.

cleared.check: Whether an ERC-4337 EntryPoint can spend or pay out a deposit booked to the PoolManager, or run the PoolManager as account or paymaster.
cleared.result: No. The EntryPoint pays a deposit out through withdrawTo to its own caller's deposit only. It uses a deposit for a user operation after the account or the paymaster answers a validation call, and src/ has no such function and no fallback, so a call from the EntryPoint to the PoolManager reverts. The PoolManager's deposit is zero on both chains.
cleared.source: https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call balanceOf(PoolManager) on the three EntryPoint addresses; src/PoolManager.sol:80-395

cleared.check: Cycle 1 lead: does the execution client source reset transient storage at the start of every transaction, including user deposits, failed deposits and rejected transactions (assumption A1).
cleared.result: Yes for every client build the chains report. revm's JournalInner clears transient_storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize, and checkpoint_revert restores transient entries. op-revm (commit 72fcf947 for Unichain, Ink and Soneium, commit 7220729 for World Chain, tag op-reth/v2.8.0 for Zora) and the Base handler (v1.5.6) end a successful or reverted transaction with commit_tx, treat a failed or halted deposit by reverting to the first checkpoint and then calling commit_tx, and call discard_tx for every other error. An unlock flag, a delta or a synced currency cannot reach the next transaction. OP Mainnet's endpoint does not report its commit, so for that chain this rests on the shared op-reth code line.

cleared.check: Whether a contract that the PoolManager calls (an unlock callback, a hook or a native payout recipient) can DELEGATECALL or CALLCODE a B20 token precompile and act on the token with the PoolManager as msg.sender.
cleared.result: No. The wrapper around every Base stateful precompile returns DelegateCallNotAllowed unless the call is a direct call. On chain, with the PoolManager as outer caller and a stub that forwards by DELEGATECALL or CALLCODE to OUSD, balanceOf and transfer revert with 0x0d89438e. With a plain CALL the token sees the stub as sender and the transfer fails for lack of balance.

cleared.check: Whether a B20 transfer made by a take survives when the surrounding call frame reverts, which would let a caller keep tokens while the PoolManager's delta is rolled back.
cleared.result: No. The precompile writes balances with EvmInternals.sstore into the revm journal, and revm commits the frame checkpoint only when the precompile result is ok and reverts it otherwise. Journal entries of an inner frame are undone when any outer frame reverts, the same as contract storage.

cleared.check: Whether anyone other than the token issuer can move the PoolManager's B20 balance: allowance, permit, factory privilege, or the shared Policy Registry.
cleared.result: No path found. transferFrom needs an allowance that only approve by the owner or a permit signed by the owner can set, and permit accepts an ECDSA signature only. The factory's privileged calls run only against a token created in the same call, guarded by TokenAlreadyExists. updatePolicy reverts with PolicyNotFound for an id that does not exist, so a token cannot point at a policy id that a stranger could later create and administer. Seize and burnBlocked need issuer roles and are covered by the cycle 1 issuer finding.

cleared.check: Whether the Base operated Activation Registry can freeze B20 tokens that the PoolManager already holds.
cleared.result: No. Activation is checked when the factory creates a token and when the Policy Registry is written. The token dispatcher checks only that the token address has code and then routes the call. Turning a feature off stops new tokens and stops list updates. It does not stop transfer or balanceOf on existing tokens.

cleared.check: Whether a currency id inside the B20 address prefix that has no token behind it (a variant byte that Base has not defined, or a valid variant that was never created) can collect credit that later becomes a claim on a real token (assumption A4).
cleared.result: No. For an undefined variant the address is a plain account without code: take succeeds and records a debt (src/types/Currency.sol:60-75), and sync reverts because balanceOf returns no data (src/types/Currency.sol:94). For an uncreated token every call reverts. A positive delta in such an id can come only from settle, which needs sync, or from a pool that already holds the id, which needs an earlier payment. No credit can exist before the token does.

cleared.check: Sweep of the Base only system addresses with msg.sender set to the PoolManager: B20 factory, Activation Registry, Policy Registry, NonceManager, TxContext, BaseTime, for empty calldata with and without value, transfer with zero and nonzero amount, balanceOf and the ten hook selectors.
cleared.result: All six revert on every shape. A take, a sync or a hook call that names one of them reverts as a whole, so nothing they do can persist. OUSD and AMDC, two live B20 tokens, answer transfer of zero with true and balanceOf with the PoolManager balance, and revert on empty calldata, on value and on the hook selectors.

cleared.check: Sweep of 38 predeploy slots, 20 precompile addresses and 26 preinstalled or reserved addresses with msg.sender set to the PoolManager and a separate tx.origin, for the call shapes P1, P2, P3 and P5: does any target accept a token style call and move value that the caller does not owe.
cleared.result: No. For P2 (transfer) the only targets that return true or empty data are real ERC-20 tokens (WETH, the governance token), addresses without code, the Safe singletons, ecrecover and P256VERIFY. The last four move nothing and the caller is still debited. For P1 (value with empty calldata) the caller is debited the full amount whatever the recipient does with it (src/PoolManager.sol:294). For P3 the targets that return 32 bytes are WETH, the governance token, LegacyERC20ETH on OP Mainnet and Zora, L1BlockNumber, the EntryPoints, sha256, ripemd160 and identity. L1BlockNumber and the three precompiles return a value that cannot change inside a transaction, so settle credits zero. The EntryPoint case is in the finding of this cycle.

cleared.check: Faces of the native asset, wrapped native: walk sync, take, settle, mint and burn across address(0) and the WETH predeploy in both orders, including a native take whose recipient is WETH.
cleared.result: Value is conserved in every order. A native take to WETH debits the caller amount in currency address(0) and mints the same amount of WETH to the PoolManager. If WETH was synced before, settle credits the caller that amount of WETH. The caller then holds a native debt and an equal WETH credit, takes the WETH, unwraps it and pays the native debt. If WETH was not synced the minted WETH stays in the PoolManager as surplus that no one can claim, and the caller still owes the ETH. A native settle while WETH is synced reverts at src/PoolManager.sol:356. Mint and burn of claims under either id need a matching credit or burn of the same id (src/PoolManager.sol:322-336).

cleared.check: Faces, tokens with more than one entry point: SNX on OP Mainnet is reachable at the proxy 0x8700dAec35aF8Ff88c16BdF0418774CB3D7599B4 and at its target 0x3f2a1f997ef089798d19473d96be484aeb3e4ecf, and the PoolManager holds 30,337 SNX. Walk sync, settle, take, mint and burn across the two ids in every order.
cleared.result: No gain in any order. The target is read only for the PoolManager: balanceOf works and transfer reverts with 'Only the proxy can call', so take under the target id always reverts and no debt in that id can be created by take. sync(target), an SNX transfer to the PoolManager and settle credit the payer under the target id for tokens it really paid. That credit can be cleared or minted as a claim and can never be paid out. The single synced currency slot is overwritten by the next sync and reset by settle (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32, src/PoolManager.sol:361), so one transfer is never credited under both ids. A real pair of working entry points would also conserve value, because each credit needs its own balance increase between a sync and a settle and each take moves the same number of units that it debits.

cleared.check: Faces, native asset with the read only LegacyERC20ETH view: orders not listed in cycle 1, namely a native take before sync(LegacyERC20ETH), and inflows that the PoolManager itself can be made to cause.
cleared.result: No gain. If the caller takes ETH first, then syncs the legacy id, forces the ETH back with SELFDESTRUCT and settles, it holds a native debt and an equal legacy credit. The legacy credit cannot leave, so the caller pays the native debt a second time. No call shape that the PoolManager can be made to send brings ETH back into it, and the PoolManager has no receive function. collectProtocolFees only lowers the balance, which makes settle revert at src/PoolManager.sol:360.

cleared.check: Whether any predeploy or precompile address can serve as a hook that returns a valid response, or that leaves a side effect after a hook call.
cleared.result: No. Of the special addresses, these have a valid flag combination under src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-126: 0x10, the BLS map to G1 precompile (afterDonate), 0x0100 P256VERIFY (afterRemoveLiquidity), L2StandardBridge 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000010 (afterDonate), SchemaRegistry 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000020 (beforeDonate) and slot 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000030 (both donate hooks). None returns 32 bytes that start with the hook selector, so the call reverts with InvalidHookResponse or HookCallFailed (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137, 152-154) and the whole operation reverts. The identity precompile would echo the selector, and its address 0x04 fails the flag check. A pool created with P256VERIFY as hook accepts liquidity and reverts on every removal. That needs LPs to pick such a pool. The Base precompile page states that P256VERIFY pricing follows EIP-7951 for equivalence with L1, so Ethereum has the same address. The case falls under the cycle 1 hook finding.

cleared.check: Whether an L1 account can act on L2 as the PoolManager, or whether code can appear at the PoolManager's address on Ethereum and use the withdrawal path.
cleared.result: No. eth_getCode on Ethereum returns empty code at all seven PoolManager addresses and their nonce is 0. A deposit from an L1 contract carries the aliased sender, and an unaliased sender needs a signature made for that address. A withdrawal that the PoolManager is made to start through L2ToL1MessagePasser carries empty data and the PoolManager's own address as target, so it gives no authority on L1.

cleared.check: Known weakness: the reth trie iterator bug fixed in November 2026 (pull request 28264). The reth v2.10.0 notes list the fix with high update priority, and the Base v1.5.3 notes say it prevents a state root mismatch. Secondary reports say a crafted transaction could trigger it and stall unpatched nodes. Do the builds these chains report contain the fix.
cleared.result: Yes. The corrected comparison (walker position equal to the seek prefix) is present at base/reth tag base-v2.5.2.11 (Base v1.5.6), at ethereum-optimism/reth tag op-v2.7.0-0 (op-reth v2.9.0-rc.1 on Unichain, Ink and Soneium) and at tag op-v2.6.0-2 (World Chain v2.8.2 and conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 on Zora). Upstream reth v2.9.0 and v2.5.1 still have the old comparison. The bug is a liveness and proof correctness issue and gives no way to move PoolManager funds. OP Mainnet is left out because its endpoint does not report a commit.

cleared.check: Cycle 1 lead: which upgrade activated the Osaka opcodes on World Chain and whether the EIP-7825 gas cap applies there.
cleared.result: Karst. op-reth v2.4.3 added the World Chain mainnet Karst time 1789992000 (21 September 2026). World Chain v2.8.2 pins an op-revm commit in which Karst maps to the Osaka instruction set. The gas cap clearance that cycle 1 gave for the other six chains therefore applies to World Chain as well: liquidity removal has no loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238) and a swap stops at the caller's price limit.

cleared.check: Cycle 1 lead on Base Transactions (type 0x79, planned for Everest): is transient storage cleared between call phases and can a failed phase leave state behind.
cleared.result: Read from source at v1.5.6. A reverting phase is undone with checkpoint_revert, which also restores transient storage, and later phases are skipped. Committed phases share transient storage with later phases. All calls in the transaction have the same msg.sender, and unlock re-locks and requires zero open deltas before it returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), so the only PoolManager state that can pass from one phase to the next is a synced currency set by the same sender. Everest has no activation date, and this must be read again at the release that activates it.

cleared.check: Whether the transient slot constants in src/ are the values their comments state, so that the lock flag, the delta counter, the synced currency and the synced reserves cannot collide with each other or with a delta slot.
cleared.result: They are. keccak256('Unlocked') - 1, keccak256('NonzeroDeltaCount') - 1, keccak256('ReservesOf') - 1 and keccak256('Currency') - 1 were recomputed and equal the constants at src/libraries/Lock.sol:8, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:9-10 and src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:11-13. Delta slots are keccak256 of a 64 byte preimage (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-16).

cleared.check: Where does the Arc client discard transient storage between two transactions of a block, and can an unlock flag, a delta or a synced currency of the PoolManager survive into the next transaction (A1)? The earlier cycle had only an RPC probe.
cleared.result: No. ArcEvm::transact_one and transact_system_call run the Arc handler, which overrides pre_execution, reward_beneficiary and validate_initial_tx_gas and leaves the rest to revm. revm-handler 18.1.0 calls journal.commit_tx in execution_result and journal.discard_tx in catch_error, and revm-context 16.0.1 clears transient_storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize. The block executor calls evm.transact for each transaction and commits the returned state. I read the main branch. The RPC reports arc/v1, so the release that mainnet runs is unconfirmed.

cleared.check: Does the USDC implementation at 0xc6ad664ac6679f4ce74e10e91449c93ec1ae3ca6, the only code that may call Native Coin Authority, let any role other than the proxy admin move or burn the native balance of an arbitrary account such as the PoolManager?
cleared.result: No. transfer moves only msg.sender's balance. transferFrom needs an allowance, and the PoolManager makes no approve call (its outbound selectors are transfer, balanceOf, unlockCallback and the hook selectors, src/types/Currency.sol:60-73 and 94, src/PoolManager.sol:110, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-134). permit and the EIP-3009 functions need an ECDSA signature of the owner or a 32 byte ERC-1271 magic value from the owner's code, and the PoolManager has no isValidSignature function and no fallback. burn destroys only the calling minter's balance. rescueERC20 moves tokens held by the token contract itself. A seizure needs an implementation upgrade by the proxy admin. The scaling by 10^12 uses SafeMath and cannot wrap for amounts below 2^127.

cleared.check: Sweep of Arc special addresses with from set to the PoolManager: empty calldata with and without value, transfer(address,uint256) with 0 and 1, balanceOf(PoolManager), the ten IHooks selectors and unlockCallback. Targets: precompiles 0x01 to 0x13 and 0x100, 0x1800...00 to ...07, the four system proxies at 0x3600...01 to ...04, the USDC proxy and implementation, the log emitter, EIP-2935, EIP-4788, EIP-7002 and EIP-7251 addresses, Memo, Multicall3From, Multicall3, Permit2, the CREATE2 factory, three EntryPoints, EURC, cirBTC, WETH, USYC and its two helpers, six CCTP contracts, both Gateway contracts, FxEscrow, the fee jar, the fee adapter, the owner contract, the Wormhole core and the Uniswap periphery.
cleared.result: No target returns a hook selector with 32 bytes that start with that selector, so none passes as a hook (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:151-153). The identity precompile echoes the calldata, and its address 0x04 carries only flag bit 2 without bit 6, which initialize rejects (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:112). transfer returns true only on USDC, EURC, cirBTC and WETH. Codeless addresses and 0x01 and 0x100 return success with empty data, which makes take a debit without a payment. balanceOf returns a constant on 0x02, 0x03 and 0x04, so sync and settle on them credit zero, and reverts or returns empty data on the other precompiles, so sync reverts. The Arc precompiles at 0x1800...00 to ...07 and the four system proxies revert on every shape. The follow-ups on the EntryPoints and the USDC implementation are recorded as findings.
cleared.source: eth_call via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io at blocks 32,582,357 to 32,584,426

cleared.check: Walk of sync, settle, take, mint and burn across three ids over one balance on Arc: address(0), the USDC proxy 0x3600 and the USDC implementation 0xc6ad..., in every order, with the deployed contract probed for value-bearing calls.
cleared.result: No double credit and no undebited payout. A native credit needs the sync slot to be zero and equals msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). With either ERC-20 id synced, settle with value reverts (line 356). sync writes currency and reserves together and sync(address(0)) clears only the currency (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32), so a stale reserve is never paired with a later currency. take debits the id it pays from before the transfer (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295). take of 0x3600 to the PoolManager itself moves nothing and still debits. On chain the deployed PoolManager rejects value on empty calldata, on sync and on unlock, returns ManagerLocked (0x54e3ca0d) for settle and settleFor outside an unlock, and accepts sync(0x3600) while locked. The implementation id adds a credit that cannot be taken and is recorded as a finding. The sub-unit rounding bound of the earlier cycle is unchanged.
cleared.source: src/PoolManager.sol:279-307 and 349-364; eth_call with a balance override via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io at block 32,584,426

cleared.check: Can a contract that gains control in the middle of a user's transaction (a hook, a token, a recipient of a native payout) use Multicall3From or Memo to call the PoolManager or USDC as that user, since CallFrom allows the transaction signer as substituted sender?
cleared.result: No. Multicall3From passes msg.sender as the sender in aggregate, aggregate3, tryAggregate and both block variants, with no caller-supplied sender. A nested contract that calls Multicall3From is itself the sender, and init_subcall rejects a sender that is neither the calling contract nor the transaction signer. CallFrom accepts calls only from Memo and Multicall3From, rejects value and rejects static context. I read the Multicall3From source in the repository and did not compare it with the deployed bytecode, and I did not read Memo.

cleared.check: Opcode differential on Arc for the patterns the PoolManager uses: CALL with value, CALLVALUE, SELFBALANCE, STATICCALL, return data, MCOPY, PUSH0, TSTORE and TLOAD, gas forwarding, calls to codeless addresses and precompile dispatch.
cleared.result: The client replaces one instruction, SELFDESTRUCT, which the PoolManager bytecode does not contain. Value-bearing frames get three extra reject conditions before revm initialises them (zero address, blocklist, recipient self-destructed in the transaction). A native payout therefore reverts only for recipients the caller chose. Calls to codeless addresses return success with empty data as on Ethereum (seen on 0x12, 0x13, the log emitter and the EIP-4788 address). Arc precompiles reject calls from the PoolManager with a revert. Everything else is revm 38 with the Osaka specification. An on-chain probe returned CALLVALUE 0, the overridden SELFBALANCE and a failing inner value call for a caller without balance.
cleared.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/evm/src/evm.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/evm/src/opcode.rs; eth_call with state overrides via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io

cleared.check: Known weaknesses of Arc: open issues 513, 514, 517 and 521 on the arc-node repository, the v0.7.0 to v0.8.0 changelog fixes, and public bug bounty notes. Can an ordinary account use any of them against funds in the PoolManager?
cleared.result: None found. Issues 513, 514 and 517 describe ways around the denylist (a pooled transaction of a newly listed sender still executes, the delegate of an EIP-7702 authorisation is not checked, the address created by a CREATE is not checked). They weaken an operator control and do not move or block PoolManager funds. Issue 521 concerns the post-quantum verifier being callable before its fork. The changelog fixes concern gas metering of precompiles, subcall accounting, SELFDESTRUCT warm state, beneficiary checks and pool hygiene. A third-party summary mentions a consensus denial of service reported through Circle's bounty programme, which is a liveness matter. I did not find a published audit report of arc-node.

cleared.check: Which interpreter runs on Tempo mainnet, where does it clear transient storage, and can PoolManager transient state cross a transaction boundary, a system call or a batch (A1)?
cleared.result: Mainnet reports v1.19.0 at commit 697ea97, whose manifest pins evm2 at revision e25a95fb. evm2 journals every TSTORE and restores it on rollback, and clears transient storage in clear_transaction_state, which runs on commit, discard, detach and drop of the executed transaction handle and on every handler error. Tempo's block executor resolves user transactions and its system calls through those paths. A type 0x76 batch runs all calls under one checkpoint with the account as caller, so only the sender's own calls share transient state. I did not establish whether the JIT backend is active on mainnet or what the v1.18.4 execution fix changed.

cleared.check: Second sweep of Tempo from the PoolManager address with the revert data classified: do any of the ten hook selectors, unlockCallback, transfer(address,uint256) or empty calldata reach a real function on a precompile, in particular on the precompiles that may pull TIP-20 from their caller without an allowance (FeeManager, StablecoinDEX, TIP20ChannelReserve)?
cleared.result: No. All thirteen selectors return UnknownFunctionSelector (0xaa4bc69a) on TIP20Factory, FeeManager, StablecoinDEX, TIP403Registry, NonceManager, both ValidatorConfig contracts, AccountKeychain, AddressRegistry, SignatureVerifier, ReceivePolicyGuard, CurrentCommittee, TIP20ChannelReserve, ZoneFactory and ZoneVerifier. StorageCredits answers only balanceOf. On a TIP-20 token the ten hook selectors and unlockCallback return UnknownFunctionSelector, so no hook selector collides with a TIP-20 function, and the dispatcher is the same for every token. Empty calldata reverts on every precompile, so the zero amount native take reaches nothing. ZoneMessenger and the ZonePortal implementation revert on every shape. The implicit pull in system_transfer_from can only be reached through functions the PoolManager cannot call.

cleared.check: Can an ordinary account make the PoolManager's TIP-20 balance rise between sync and settle without paying the same amount, or fall without a take (A2)? I listed every balance write in the TIP-20 precompile and simulated transfers from the PoolManager to special recipients.
cleared.result: No path found. Credits come from _transfer (matched by a debit of the sender), _mint (issuer role), the fee refund (fee payer, which must sign) and claim_rewards (msg.sender). The PoolManager cannot sign and cannot call claimRewards. A self transfer from the PoolManager returns true and leaves the balance unchanged, because the debit and the credit each read the stored balance. Debits of the PoolManager need its own transfer call, an allowance or a permit signature it cannot produce, or an issuer burn. Spending limits are skipped when the from address is not tx.origin, so a limited signer of the attacker cannot make PoolManager payouts revert for others.

cleared.check: Can a third party set a receive policy for the PoolManager or for the Uniswap periphery on Tempo, so that payments into them are diverted to ReceivePolicyGuard with the attacker as recovery authority?
cleared.result: Not for the PoolManager. setReceivePolicy(uint64,uint64,address) acts on msg.sender and has no account argument, and the PoolManager can only emit the selectors transfer, balanceOf, unlockCallback and the hook selectors, all of which the registry rejects. receivePolicy is unset for the PoolManager, PositionManager, both Universal Routers, Permit2, Multicall3, Quoter, CreateX and the three EntryPoints at block 50,287,321. A contract that forwards arbitrary calls, such as Multicall3, can be made to set its own policy by anyone. Whether a periphery contract has such a path is left as a lead.

cleared.check: The earlier cycle cleared the native branch on Tempo from documentation. Does the interpreter itself refuse value, and what do CALLVALUE, SELFBALANCE and BALANCE return inside a call?
cleared.result: An eth_call with override code returned 0 for CALLVALUE, SELFBALANCE and BALANCE(PoolManager), and an inner CALL with 1 wei from an account without balance returned 0. With a balance override the same call succeeded, so the interpreter applies the normal balance check and the native branch of take and settle is inert because no account holds a native balance (src/types/Currency.sol:44-52, src/PoolManager.sol:352-354). A positive address(0) delta would in any case have nothing to draw on, since the PoolManager's native balance is zero.
cleared.source: eth_call with state overrides via https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz at block 50,285,768

cleared.check: Standard precompile addresses as currencies or hooks on Tempo and Arc: can sync and settle create a positive delta, or can a hook call be answered, at 0x01 to 0x11 and 0x100?
cleared.result: No. balanceOf(PoolManager) returns a fixed hash on 0x02 and 0x03 and the echoed calldata on 0x04, so the difference between sync and settle is zero. 0x01, 0x05 and 0x100 return empty data and 0x06 to 0x11 revert, so sync reverts when it decodes the result (src/types/Currency.sol:94). transfer returns empty data on 0x01 and 0x100, which take treats as success and which only debits the caller (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). On the deployed PoolManagers sync succeeds for 0x02 and reverts for 0x01, 0x100 and the codeless 0x12 on Arc, and on Tempo it reverts for an unused TIP-20 address, for the FeeManager and for the codeless ConfigurableAccount address. The identity precompile is the only address that echoes a hook selector, and 0x04 is no valid hook address.
cleared.source: eth_call via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io and https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127

cleared.check: Known weaknesses of Tempo: an automated audit write-up of the reference contracts, the T3 fix bundle TIP-1038, two TIP-20 dispatcher fixes, and the node release notes from v1.17.0 to v1.19.0. Can an ordinary account use any of them against PoolManager funds?
cleared.result: None found. The audit write-up reports that expired session signers could still spend within their limit in a reference contract, which concerns the signer's own account. TIP-1038 added pause checks to mint and burn and to StablecoinDEX swaps, which are issuer and exchange matters. Pull requests 1790 and 3535 made mutable calls to uninitialised TIP-20 addresses revert and stopped an out-of-gas condition from being reported as an uninitialised token, which matches the Uninitialized revert seen on chain. The v1.18.2 and v1.18.4 notes mention EVM changes without detail and remain a lead. The repository's security page says audits are ongoing and no bounty is active.

cleared.check: A5 on Tempo and Arc: does any protocol rule read a token or native balance during a transaction and grant something that outlasts it, so that funds taken from the PoolManager for one unlock have value?
cleared.result: None found. Tempo charges fees from the fee payer before execution and refunds after it, classifies payment transactions by their calls, grants storage credits for cleared slots and has no stake in TIP-20 tokens. Arc validators are permissioned through a system contract and fees are debited from the sender before execution. In both cases a balance held only inside an unlock is back in the PoolManager before any of these rules reads it. I did not read the Fee AMM and StablecoinDEX code for flash-style use, which would be ordinary use of borrowed funds and must still be repaid before unlock returns (src/PoolManager.sol:112).
